item.title: Seabird ‘spies’ could help spot ships that aren’t broadcasting their location
item.description: A northern gannet ( Morus bassanus ) tagged with biologging devices on its back and tail Steve Votier Audio from seabirds fitted with mini recording devices and GPS trackers has been used by researchers to show that marine life can record encounters with vessels that are otherwise difficult to track. Many large vessels are now legally required to carry automatic identification systems broadcasting their identity and location at regular intervals. Although this has allowed interactions between animals and fisheries to be studied at scale, there are enormous gaps in coverage. In fact, recent research suggests that three-quarters of industrial fishing vessels don’t use the technology, says Jonathan Rutter at the University of Oxford. This is partly because regulations on the types of vessels that are required to share data vary by country. Large satellite ‘blind spots’ also contribute to the problem, he says, and so does subterfuge for the purpose of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing (IUU). Advertisement Read more Most large fishing boats go untracked as ‘dark vessels’ Rutter says that being caught as bycatch in fishing is one of the greatest risks to seabird populations, but if fishing vessels are only tracked “with conventional methods, such footprints of risk may be strikingly incomplete”. The team analysed audio collected from devices attached to seven northern gannets ( Morus bassanus ) and found that one third of the audio detections couldn’t be matched with vessel tracking data – mostly off the UK coast. Overall, 12 per cent of the vessel detections made by the four critically endangered Balearic shearwaters ( Puffinus mauretanicus ) included in the study couldn’t be matched to public data. But given the high vessel density where they were – off the Catalan coast – the researchers estimated that up to 20 per cent of the vessels detected by the four birds weren’t broadcasting their identity. Tammy Davies at BirdLife International – a global partnership of non-governmental organisations – who wasn’t involved in the study, says the research could “give us a more complete picture of the risks seabirds face at sea” and “ultimately, this could contribute to better assessments of bycatch risk and help identify fisheries and areas where conservation measures are most needed”. Peter Ejbye-Ernst at the Netherlands Institute for the Study of Crime and Law Enforcement (NSCR), describes the study as “fascinating” from a green criminology point of view, too. A tagged northern gannet coming in to land in Wales Steve Votier “What this study is somewhat proposing is that we can also look outside of humans for witnesses too,” he says, which overcomes a key barrier in observing crime at sea. item.title: SpaceX Starship debris becomes art in Ashley Zelinskie's 'The Weight of Space' (video, photos)
item.description: null When a SpaceX Starship broke apart over Turks and Caicos in Jan. 2025, pieces of its heat shield washed ashore. Some of that material now hangs on a gallery wall in New York City, embedded in artist Ashley Zelinskie's print of the very explosion it survived. Look closely at the print and you can see little flakes on the surface. Some of Zelinskie's friends vacationing on the islands had come across pieces of heat-shield tile. "I think you might want these," Zelinskie recalled one friend telling her. She did. The Brooklyn-based artist ground the fragments into dust and worked them into the print. Ashley Zelinskie incorporated dust from recovered SpaceX Starship heat-shield tiles into this print of the vehicle breaking apart over Turks and Caicos. (Image credit: Ashley Zelinskie) The Starship print is part of "Ejecta," which captures rocket plumes and explosions on paper. It's one of four series in Zelinskie's solo exhibition, "The Weight of Space," which opened Nov. 20 at Heft Gallery in Manhattan. Her marble sculptures in "Monuments" depict the Hubble Space Telescope, retired NASA astronaut Mike Massimino's spaceflight gear and more. Five "Launch Sequence" sculptures follow a rocket through liftoff, and the interactive "Crowded Sky" lets visitors track what's currently orbiting overhead in real time. Zelinskie gave Space.com Editor-in-Chief Tariq Malik and me a tour before the gallery doors opened. Massimino joined her that evening to celebrate the exhibition and their collaboration on "Monuments." You can watch the tour in the video above. Monuments Massimino turned up in our first look at Zelinskie's work, too. In 2022, I photographed the two of them beside her "Exploration JWST" sculpture at "Unfolding the Universe: First Light," an exhibit inspired by the James Webb Space Telescope's first images. Four years later, Massimino stood in a New York gallery looking at another Zelinskie sculpture. "That's my arm there," he told Malik. Artist Ashley Zelinskie and Space.com Editor-in-Chief Tariq Malik discuss the sculpture between them, which depicts astronaut Mike Massimino’s bare hand gripping a replica of the handrail he pulled off the Hubble Space Telescope in 2009. (Image credit: Future/Steve Spaleta) In that hand is a piece of hardware Malik remembers watching Massimino wrestle with in real time. During NASA's final Hubble servicing mission in 2009, a stripped bolt left a handrail blocking access to the telescope's Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph (STIS). Mission Control instructed Massimino to forcibly remove the handrail so he and fellow spacewalker Michael Good could get on with the repair. Massimino told Malik that pulling the handrail off Hubble brought back a childhood memory of his father and his Uncle Frank driving a long screwdriver through a stuck oil filter. item.title: Marlins Hand Out 1,000 Meals To Miami Families On Friday
item.description: Credit: Jasen Vinlove-USA TODAY Sports On Friday at loanDepot Park, 1,000 South Florida families received holiday meals distributed by two hundred volunteers. Marlins president of baseball operations Peter Bendix brought his 7-month-old son to the event, according to MLB.com . The baby wore a turkey onesie while his father helped organize the distribution. This annual event marks the 18th year the team has fed local families before Thanksgiving. The team did not just drop off boxes and leave. They set up stations where families could grab turkeys, beans, rice, and stuffing mix. Volunteers also handed out pasta, tomato sauce, canned vegetables, and even protein shakes. Marlins president of business Caroline O’Connor stood at the turkey station to help. She noted that the event grows larger every single year because the team gets closer to the people. Money and Meals for Neighbors The financial support went beyond just food on a plate. Feeding South Florida was presented with a check for $48,890 as part of the initiative. This money helps the charity buy more food for the region throughout the year. About 150 Marlins employees and 50 workers from Amazon joined forces to make it happen. The group also gave out 400 extra turkeys around Miami-Dade County earlier in the week. First-time dad Bendix said the event matters deeply to his own family. “It’s such a great family event, and it’s such a great thing that we do as the Marlins to help families in the local community,” Bendix said. He added that providing for the community is a huge part of their family life. “Having our own family is something that’s really important to us, and being able to help provide for the community is a huge part of that.” Leadership and Local Support Local leaders showed up to thank the volunteers and see the work firsthand. Miami-Dade County mayor Daniella Levine Cava and City of Miami Commissioner Rolando Escalona attended the event. Escalona said the food distribution helps families who need it most. “This goes a very long way,” Escalona said, “so I’m extremely grateful for this event.” The partnership received praise from Giovanni Castro, who leads Amazon’s state and local public policy efforts. He said the team shows they are more than a ballclub. “For three years, Amazon has been a proud partner with the Marlins, and every time this team shows they’re more than a ballclub. They’re a neighbor who shows up for all of South Florida.” The story was excerpted from Christina De Nicola’s Marlins Beat newsletter.

item.title: Tottenham Must Not Waste Another Academy Prospect
item.description: Luca Williams-Barnett celebrates after scoring the first goal during the FA Premier League match between Tottenham Hotspur FC and Ipswich Town FC. Credit IMAGO / Propaganda Photo Recording Date 21.11.2026 Media ID 1086192367 | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Barry Dixon, LWOF Site Manager Tottenham Hotspur have moved quickly to secure young sensation Luca Williams-Barnett’s future after the teenager signed a new contract with the club. The 18-year-old has been integrated into the first team under Roberto De Zerbi, impressing in pre-season and off the bench against Crystal Palace before making his first Premier League start against Ipswich Town, when he scored and assisted in the 2-0 win. Having joined Spurs at Under-10 level, his progression into the senior side is an example of what the academy can produce. However, Williams-Barnett’s new deal should be the beginning of a long and successful Tottenham career, rather than another case of a player slipping through the fingers of the north London club. Read More: Ipswich Performance Gives Roberto De Zerbi Selection Headaches Tottenham Must Give Williams-Barnett a Genuine First-Team Opportunity Spurs Have Struggled to Turn Potential Into First-Team Regulars Tottenham’s academy has produced some outstanding players over the years, with Harry Kane, Ledley King and Glenn Hoddle among the most famous to enjoy successful careers in north London. More recently, the likes of Kyle Walker-Peters, Harry Winks, Japhet Tanganga and Oliver Skipp all progressed through the ranks to become regular first-team players before moving to pastures new. However, it has become more difficult for Spurs to produce and retain academy graduates in recent times. Several youngsters have made their senior debuts in the last three seasons, such as Jamie Donley, Damola Ajayi, Callum Olusesi, Alfie Dorrington, Jun’ai Byfield and James Rowswell, but none have been given a real chance to show their ability in the first-team setup. Mikey Moore is another who has enjoyed a more regular involvement with the first team, especially during 2024/25, and is continuing his development out on loan, first with Rangers last season and now with FC Koln, as he hopes to add to his 22 Spurs appearances. Of course, playing young players can be a gamble and many never reach the required standard for Premier League football. However, Spurs must ensure the likes of Williams-Barnett and Moore are utilised properly with a long-term vision, rather than simply giving them the odd appearance before they seek a route out of the club. IMAGO / News Images The Ones Who Have Slipped Through the Net There are also examples of players who could have been given more of an opportunity before being allowed to leave, something Spurs must avoid if they are to get the best from their young players. item.title: Brandon Aiyuk signs in Washington, officially ending 49ers drama
item.description: The NFL future of Brandon Aiyuk has finally been decided, with the veteran wide receiver reportedly signing with the Washington Commanders following his messy departure from the San Francisco 49ers. According to NFL insider Adam Schefter, Aiyuk is joining Washington’s practice squad, with his agent Drew Rosenhaus confirming the move. The signing also gives Aiyuk an opportunity to reunite with former college teammate Jayden Daniels, who is now the Commanders’ starting quarterback. Free-agent WR Brandon Aiyuk is signing with the Washington Commanders practice squad, per his agent Drew Rosenhaus. Aiyuk once again becomes teammates with his Commanders QB Jayden Daniels. https://t.co/jt8diY95o3 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 25, 2026 BREAKING: Brandon Aiyuk is joining the Commanders practice squad, per his agent. The former 49ers WR is set to reunite with college teammate Jayden Daniels after clearing waivers. His offseason wishes come true. 🎥: brandonaiyuk/IG https://t.co/vM5JCJopvL — Complex Sports (@ComplexSports) November 25, 2026 The 28-year-old was released by San Francisco on Monday before passing through waivers unclaimed on Tuesday, allowing him to sign with a new organization. His departure officially brings an end to a complicated relationship with the 49ers that deteriorated over the past two seasons. MORE: Eagles’ Joe Milton details Dak Prescott’s impact on him ahead of Thanksgiving Day matchup Aiyuk’s complicated 49ers departure Dec 17, 2023; Glendale, Arizona, USA; San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk (11) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports Aiyuk had originally signed a contract extension with San Francisco ahead of the 2024 season, but his campaign was cut short after suffering a torn ACL in mid-October. The wide receiver subsequently missed the entire 2025 season amid conflicting reports surrounding his health and recovery. The 49ers eventually voided his contract guarantees ahead of the 2025 campaign before placing him on the Reserve/Left Squad list in December. San Francisco general manager John Lynch appeared to acknowledge that Aiyuk’s time with the organization was finished when he addressed the situation in January 2026. “I think it’s safe to say played his last snap with the 49ers,” Lynch said. Aiyuk was officially reinstated from the Reserve/Left Squad list on November 9, giving the 49ers a two-week window to determine whether they wanted to retain him. The organization ultimately decided to release the veteran receiver. item.title: Three keys to a Gopher win over Wisconins and how to watch
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 03: Minnesota Golden Gophers defensive lineman TJ Bush Jr. (3) celebrates pressuring Michigan Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood (19) which lead to an interception during the second half to the college football game between the Michigan Wolverines and the Minnesota Golden Gophers on October 3rd, 2026, at Huntington Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A Black Friday evening matchup in primetime for the 136th matchup between the Gophers and Badgers. A monumental game for both programs trying to finish the season strong. How to Watch TV: NBC Time: 6:30 Stream: Peacock PJ Fleck and the Gophers have won four of the last five matchups with Wisconsin. Can Fleck maintain his dominance over the Badgers to make it five out of six? KEYS TO A GOPHER WIN Stop all the runs – Darrion Dupree is coming off a 125-yard game at Purdue and quarterback Colton Joseph rushed for 187 yards. Stop the running backs, stop the quarterback and make Joseph pass the ball. Taking proper angles and wrapping up with solid tackling has not been a strength of this Gopher defense, but they have to find a way on Friday night. Punt returns for field position – I noticed that the Wisconsin punter has only 9 fair catches this season. For context, Tom Weston has 20. This indicates to me that punt returns will be available for Javon Tracy. Can he break one again and either give us some points or set up the offense to score? Find an offensive identity – It is the final game of the season so I realize how unlikely this is, BUT FOR GOD’S SAKE, find something to hang your hat on offensively. I do think that Drake Lindsey and whoever was calling plays got into a better rhythm in the second half last week, so maybe they’ve found a little something. And Lindsey’s two touchdown passes plus the strike to Noah Jennings down the sidelines to set up the game-winning field goal were some of the best passes he has thrown in weeks. So maybe? OPPOSING PLAYERS TO WATCH #1 QB – Colton Joseph – I am much more concerned about his legs than I am his arm. But he is the one to be most concerned with on offense. #8 LB – Mason Posa – A sophomore, coming off of a freshman All-American season. He is going to be a problem. PREDICTION I am feeling overly confident heading into this game. Wisconsin is not what they appear and I think that PJ gets unusually (yet appropriately) aggressive. Is this going to be a blowout? No chance. But are we going to shut down the Badger offense and do enough on offense to get the win? Absolutely. Minnesota – 31 Wisconsin – 17

item.title: Green light for Starmind: SpaceX gets approval to deploy 1 million AI satellites
item.description: null Earth orbit could get a lot more crowded in the coming years. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) just granted SpaceX approval to deploy one million of its Starmind AI data-center satellites in orbit. "This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth," FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said today (Nov. 25) in a statement announcing the approval. AI has become central to SpaceX's business plans and identity over the past year or so. For example, the company has said that it's eyeing a "total addressable market" of $28.5 trillion over the long haul — and nearly $23 trillion of that is in "enterprise AI applications." Starmind is key to those lofty ambitions. SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk believes that the future of AI compute is in space, where energy (from the sun ) is unlimited and there are no land-owning neighbors to lodge NIMBY complaints. SpaceX aims to launch the first of its Starmind satellites in the third quarter of 2027. The spacecraft will fly on the company's fully reusable Starship megarocket, which has deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink satellites on its most recent two test flights . Those 52 spacecraft are the vanguard of another enormous constellation: Musk has said that the next-gen Starlink network will eventually consists of about 100,000 satellites . The planned numbers for Starlink and Starmind are truly mind-boggling. To put them into perspective: Since the dawn of the space age in 1957, humanity has launched a total of just 28,000 satellites, give or take a few hundred. And the biggest constellation ever operated to date, the current iteration of Starlink, consists of about 11,000 spacecraft. These coming buildouts will require an enormous number of launches. Starship can carry a maximum of 60 V3 Starlink satellites per launch, for instance, so it will take about 1,700 liftoffs just to assemble that network (and more to maintain it, as the operational life of each satellite is expected to be about five years). Putting so many satellites into orbit also raises the risks of collisions. SpaceX has proven to be extremely proficient in this regard with its current Starlink satellites, which can detect and avoid potential collisions autonomously. But more evasive maneuvers will be required as space gets more and more crowded. SpaceX isn't the only company that aims to operate data centers in space; Cowboy Space , Starcloud, Blue Origin and Google, among other companies, have voiced similar ambitions. Starcloud and Google , in fact, have already launched AI pathfinder satellites. "Compute campuses or data centers are essential to sustaining America's leadership in SI," Carr said in the same statement. ("SI" stands for super intelligence, the Trump administration's preferred term for AI.) item.title: ‘He’s finished’ – Barcelona fans continue to express concern over one player during Sabah clash
item.description: ‘He’s finished’ – Barcelona fans continue to express concern over one player during Sabah clash Supporters of La Liga giants Barcelona have on Wednesday moved to express their collective concern regarding the ongoing exploits of a member of the club’s midfield ranks. The Blaugrana star in question? Gavi. Spanish international Gavi was for his part afforded a rare opportunity to impress from the off this evening. After Barcelona made the trip to Baku to lock horns with Sabah in the Champions League, the 22-year-old was handed just his third start of the campaign. Gavi’s efforts to justify his inclusion, however, have since come up some way short… From his berth in the middle of the park, the youngster has struggled to impact the game in any meaningful manner, either going forward or whilst defending. Against one of the weaker opponents their side will meet this season, those of a Blaugrana persuasion have therefore been quick to express their collective worry about Gavi’s form. Some, in fact, have gone as far as to label the midfielder as ‘finished’. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Boston Celtics back after 131-116 NBA Cup win over Washington Wizards
item.description: The Boston Celtics are back after their 131-116 NBA Cup win over the Washington Wizards on this past Monday (Nov. 25) night. Or at least that is the point of view of the hosts of the "How Bout Them Celtics!" podcast, Jack Simone and Sam LaFrance, who took some time on a recent episode of their show to talk over how Boston snapped their four-game win streak (the longest yet of the Joe Mazzulla era) with their win vs Washington in NBA Cup action. An 80-point first half made the argument for them, but a rough third quarter did a lot of work undermining said argument. Are the Celtics really back after this won vs. the lowly wiz, or is there still plenty of work for Boston to do if they want to stay in the win column moving forward? Take a look at the clip embedded below to hear what they had to say about all of the above and then some. item.title: Rams GM Makes Clear Statement on Potential WR Additions
item.description: Support Local Media - Click to Add LA Sports Report as a Preferred Source on Google The Los Angeles Rams encountered some injury trouble among their wide receivers this season, but general manager Les Snead isn’t looking to add anyone else this season. The Rams’ top two receivers in Puka Nacua and Davante Adams are out, with the former set to miss the remainder of the season after undergoing MCL surgery. Several options are open for the Rams, such as former 1,000-yard receiver Brandon Aiyuk, but Snead isn’t going to pursue anyone else. “Like I tell people all the time, it’s not Madden,” Snead said on the Coach McVay Show. “You don’t just acquire someone – in Madden, you don’t have to teach them the playbook.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by LA Sports Report (@lasportsreport) While Snead hasn’t shied away from big midseason moves in the past, acquiring players like Jalen Ramsey, Von Miller and Sony Michel with blockbuster trades in years past, he doesn’t often add to the offense midway through the season. With the deadline already behind them, any further additions for the Rams could impact their results. Nov 1, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams president Kevin Demoff (left), general manager Les Snead (center) and owner Stan Kroenke watch during the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Who Are the Rams’ Receiving Options? Behind Nacua and Adams, the Rams’ top receiver on the season is tight end Tyler Higbee, who has less than half of Nacua’s yards and more than 150 fewer than Adams. The Rams’ next leading pass catcher is running back Kyren Williams, closely followed by Konata Mumpfield with 243 yards. Mumpfield led the Rams in receiving yards in their last game, a win against the Arizona Cardinals, logging three catches for 81 yards on the day. Veteran Tutu Atwell also figures to get more looks with Adams and Nacua sidelined, but he only caught one pass for 31 yards against the Cardinals. Who Do the Rams Play Next? Following their bye week, the Rams will face the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday at 5:00 p.m. PT. Both teams are 6-4, but the Rams come in with all of the momentum having won each of their last four games. The Packers and Rams both got an abbreviated bye week, lasting just 10 days rather than the standard 14, but are sure to be energized as they chase spots in the playoffs. The post Rams GM Makes Clear Statement on Potential WR Additions appeared first on LA Sports Report .

item.title: Insider sees a troubling path to Puka Nacua’s next Rams deal
item.description: Puka Nacua might have played his final game in a Los Angeles Rams uniform. He also might not have. ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter weighed in on Nacua’s future during Tuesday’s episode of “The Adam Schefter Podcast.” “Here’s what I would say: He’s an unrestricted free agent ! And he’s an unrestricted free agent coming off a knee injury . I think they want to keep him. I think they plan to keep him. Will they actually keep him? We’ll see,” Schefter said. ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter stands on the field prior to an NFL wild-card playoff football game in Houston, Saturday, Jan. 4, 2020. AP “The offseason, there’s a lot of things that come up. Puka obviously is serving a suspension now , he had off-the-field issues last offseason, now he’s got a knee injury that was operated on,” Schefter added. “He’s coming off the knee, he’s a free agent, there has been a suspension; the Rams would like him back. He’s gonna want to get paid… so how is this all gonna work out? I think it’s a mistake to say he’s not back in LA, and I think it’s a mistake to say it’s automatically [back]. We don’t know!” Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (12) warms up before an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers in Inglewood, Calif., Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. AP Photo/Caroline Brehman Schefter believes the Rams plan to keep Nacua. Whether the two sides can agree on a price remains an open question. Losing Nacua would leave a sizable hole in the Rams’ passing game. He’s developed into one of the NFL’s best receivers in Los Angeles. Puka Nacua of the Los Angeles Rams enters the field before a game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, Nov. 1, 2026. Getty Images Los Angeles still has a season it needs to focus on, including a critical game against the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night. But Nacua’s contract situation will become the biggest story to follow for the Rams once their 2026-27 campaign concludes.

item.title: Badgers reclaim number one ahead of non-conference series thanks to buzzer beater
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - APRIL 11: Daniel Hauser #31 of the Wisconsin Badgers is consoled by teammates after the Denver Pioneers defeated the Wisconsin Badgers during the Division I Men's Ice Hockey Championship held at T-Mobile Arena on April 11, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Tyler Schank/NCAA Photos via Getty Images) | NCAA Photos via Getty Images Super, scintillating, sensational. Dick Vitale’s three S’s came to mind watching the Wisconsin Badgers take down the Penn State Nittany Lions last weekend. They might not be the most dangerous foe in the conference right now, but they always seem to give the Badgers problems. And following their first loss against Ohio State the week before, Wisconsin could ill-afford problems. Both games were decided by just one goal, but No. 1 Wisconsin (10-1-1, 6-1-1 Big Ten) won them in very different ways, with junior Gavin Morrissey bookending the series with huge plays. We want MORRissey goals! 🍎: Finn Brink pic.twitter.com/e55Q2PW0eM — Wisconsin Hockey (@BadgerMHockey) November 21, 2026 Penn State (2-11-1, 0-7-1 Big Ten) is not having a great year, but for what it’s worth, they’ve split their last eight games with the Badgers. Morrissey fired a shot across the bow early as the Nittany Lions were on the power play Friday night. Sophomore Finn Brink chased down an errant pass off the boards in the defensive zone and slapped the puck ahead to a streaking Morrissey, who patiently handled the puck until the goaltender opened his pads and gave up the five-hole. After Penn State answered in the waning moments of the second period, it was Vasily Zelenov who cleaned up a loose rebound less than two minutes into the third period to claim the game-winning goal. Zelenov is averaging a point per game in his sophomore season and centering the second line tremendously as a key contributor, currently second on the team in assists behind only Morrissey. Saturday night is when the fireworks came into play. After Zach Wooten and JJ Wiebusch scored first-period goals sandwiched around a tally for Penn State’s Justin Poirier, the Badgers maintained their 2-1 lead for most of the game, despite bombarding the Nittany Lions to the tune of 20 shots in the second period. With just over six minutes to go, Penn State found the equalizer. It started to look like the Badgers might need overtime to try and earn the extra point and avoid a clean sweep over a team yet to win in conference play. Then chaos ensued. Things began with Gavin Morrissey winning an improbable offensive zone faceoff with ten seconds remaining. Seriously, he was horizontal and completely off his skates when he had the awareness to tap the puck back to Joe Palodichuk and move it around the horn. Palodichuk then found Hensler with a less-than-perfect pass, who corralled the puck with his skate and was barely able to redirect it toward the net. item.title: Aaron Rodgers, several Steelers ‘frustrated’ with Mike McCarthy
item.description: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The fallout of the Steelers’ decision to bench Aaron Rodgers continues as Wednesday morning turns into Wednesday afternoon. The Steelers are now getting Mason Rudolph prepared to start his first game of the season this Friday when they take on the Broncos. Amidst the whirlwind of the news, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports that the relationship between Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy has grown strained. “The relationship between Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy has not been in a good place, and a path back together is considered ‘highly unlikely,’” Schultz reports. Additionally, it isn’t just Rodgers who has grown frustrated with McCarthy. Multiple other offensive players have, as well, according to Schultz. “The frustration is not just with Rodgers,” Schultz writes. “Multiple position groups have been upset, and I’m told McCarthy has not been what some offensive players hoped for. Frustration has been growing among everyone for weeks. The Rodgers benching is just the start of what’s being revealed publicly. I’ve also heard players who were used to having Mike Tomlin have struggled with the change.” It certainly sounds like this is just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the internal frustrations and dysfunction as it pertains to this Steelers team. item.title: Brazil U17s begin preparations for Costa Rica after beating Tanzania
item.description: Brazil U17s begin preparations for Costa Rica after beating Tanzania Preparations underway for the clash Credits: Nelson Terme /CBF Brazil's men's U-17 national team began preparations this Wednesday (25) for their clash with Costa Rica in the third round of group-stage matches at the U-17 World Cup. It was the team's first training session since their 1-0 win over Tanzania, a result that secured Brazil's place in the second round with a match to spare. Players who played more than 45 minutes against Tanzania underwent a recovery session. The session at Al Thumama featured rondo drills with players moving in and out, along with acceleration and speed work. The players then took part in competitive drills, finishing each move with a shot on goal. The session concluded with technical and fitness drills involving shooting, crossing and attacking situations. This Thursday (26), the national team will get back to work for their final training session before facing Costa Rica. The session will wrap up coach Carlos Eduardo Patetuci's team's preparations for the third round of World Cup group-stage matches. Brazil and Costa Rica face off on Friday (27) at 5 p.m. local time (11 a.m. Brasília time) at the Aspire Zone Complex in Doha. item.title: Saraki cautions Kwara Gov over treatment of traditional rulers
item.description: Former Senate President, Dr Abubakar Bukola Saraki, has urged Kwara State Governor Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq to respect traditional rulers and allow them receive political leaders across party lines. Saraki made the call following allegations that the governor had summoned some traditional rulers to Ilorin and threatened to suspend those who received leaders of the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) during courtesy visits to their palaces. In a statement personally signed by him, Saraki said the alleged actions followed his stakeholder engagements in Kwara North Senatorial District, which began last week. He explained that visits to traditional rulers were part of established customs and protocols, adding that the royal fathers should be allowed to receive political leaders regardless of their party affiliations. Saraki said traditional rulers were fathers of all and should not be subjected to pressure over their interactions with politicians. He also urged the leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to caution Abdulrazaq, saying political differences should not prevent opposition parties from engaging communities and traditional institutions. The former Senate President recalled that during the 16 years the PDP governed Kwara State, traditional rulers were not prevented from receiving opposition leaders. He said democracy required tolerance of opposing views and urged the governor to respect the state’s traditional institutions. Saraki, however, insisted that the alleged actions would not discourage the PDP from continuing its engagements across the state. He said the party would sustain its outreach to communities in the three senatorial districts, adding that the response to its engagements had been encouraging. Saraki also urged the leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to call the governor to order, saying his alleged conduct was inconsistent with the democratic principles of the party. item.title: Switzerland Picks 57 Countries for Crypto Tax Data Sharing Starting in 2028
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Switzerland Picks 57 Countries for Crypto Tax Data Sharing Starting in 2028 Switzerland’s Federal Council has approved 57 countries and territories with which the country plans to automatically share tax information on crypto users starting in 2028, extending its long-standing bank data exchange to bitcoin and other digital assets. The list includes all European Union member states, the United Kingdom and various G20 countries, the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) said in a release on Wednesday. The exchange will run under the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, known as CARF. With the decision, Switzerland intends to implement the crypto exchange at the same time as other global asset management centers, according to the release. The government did not name the 57 jurisdictions beyond those broad groups, and it did not publish the full list alongside the announcement. Exchanges only with partners that qualify Data will not flow to every name on the list. An exchange will take place only if a partner jurisdiction wants to swap information with Switzerland and meets the conditions of the OECD standard, in particular its requirements on confidentiality and data security. Before any financial account or crypto data changes hands, the Federal Council will run a targeted check of whether each partner complies with OECD standards. It will rely on a review mechanism Parliament approved on Sept. 28, 2026, which covers both the older exchange of bank account data and the new crypto exchange. The domestic legal basis for the crypto exchange took effect on Jan. 1, 2026. Earlier this month, though, the SIF said the framework could not be implemented before Jan. 1, 2027, because the partner list still needed approval and notifications had to go to the OECD. The rules do not apply this year. The Council also approved Armenia and Rwanda as new partners for the exchange of financial account information, with first exchanges due in 2028, and signed off on two notifications needed to carry out the exchange. Both partner lists were broadly supported during public consultations in 2024 and 2025, the government said. Down from 74 partners The final list is shorter than first planned. In June 2025, the Federal Council proposed 74 countries relevant to the crypto market, including all EU states, the UK and most G20 members. That plan left out the United States and Saudi Arabia, and it targeted a 2026 start with first data exchanges in 2027. Wednesday’s release did not say which countries were dropped or whether the U.S. is now on the list. The U.S. has committed to begin CARF exchanges by 2029, according to the OECD’s Global Forum, which lists Switzerland among 27 jurisdictions aiming for first exchanges by 2028. That U.S. timeline is already shaping policy elsewhere. South Korea pushed its 22% crypto tax back to 2029 partly because it will not receive American crypto trading data

item.title: Senate Appropriations Committee session turns violent as aide, security operatives clash
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — A legislative aide to Senator Allwell Onyesoh (Rivers East) was allegedly assaulted by security operatives attached to the Senate Committee on Appropriations, chaired by Senator Olamilekan Adeola (APC, Ogun West), during a confrontation at the National Assembly complex, Abuja. The aide, Barrister Kingsley Wali, reportedly sustained head injuries during the incident and was rushed to the National Assembly Clinic for medical attention. Wali alleged that he and another aide to Senator Onyesoh, identified as Dr Kingsley, were attacked by security personnel after accompanying their principal to an Appropriations Committee meeting. Recounting the incident, Wali said the confrontation occurred after Senator Onyesoh had entered the committee room and he attempted to follow him. He said security personnel at the entrance were trying to close the door and stopped him from entering. According to him, when the operatives attempted to push his colleague away, he explained that their principal had already entered the room and that they were not attempting to force their way inside. He alleged that the situation escalated when the security personnel grabbed Dr Kingsley by the neck and began assaulting him. “I kept telling them to leave him alone because he is our senator’s personal assistant and my colleague. I even held one of the security personnel’s hands and pleaded with him to stop beating him,” Wali said. He further alleged that the operatives turned on him because he intervened on behalf of his colleague. Wali claimed that one of the security personnel grabbed him and pushed him down a staircase, while three others allegedly cornered him and repeatedly hit his head with the butt of a gun. He said the assault continued until he slumped, after which the operatives left him. According to him, Dr Kingsley subsequently took photographs of his condition and sent them to Senator Onyesoh through WhatsApp while the senator was attending the committee meeting. Wali said the senator came out after receiving the photographs and found him lying in a pool of blood. He added that the senator subsequently took him into the committee room, where members expressed shock at his condition and directed that he be taken to the hospital for treatment. Speaking about his condition, Wali said he was still weak following the alleged assault and the fall. “I’m weak. I’m completely weak because they pushed me down and I slumped. But God will take care of everything. I thank God for everything,” he said. However, Senator Adeola’s Special Adviser on Media, Kayode Odunaro, offered a different account of the incident. In a statement titled, “Security Breach at Senate Committee on Appropriations Room,” Odunaro said the confrontation followed a misunderstanding between aides of some senators attempting to gain access to a committee room during a closed-door session and security personnel stationed at the entrance. He said the incident occurred without the knowledge

item.title: Bithumb Says October Hack Exposed Passports, Bank Accounts and Wallet Addresses
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bithumb Says October Hack Exposed Passports, Bank Accounts and Wallet Addresses South Korean crypto exchange Bithumb said Wednesday that an October hack of its internal systems exposed more people and far more personal data than it first disclosed, including passport numbers, bank account numbers and crypto wallet addresses. The exchange also said the intruder had access for about 15 days before being shut out, not the roughly one hour it reported last month. In an updated notice posted Nov. 25, Bithumb said a follow-up review of the breach of Daou Office, its internal mobile groupware system, turned up additional affected people and additional types of data. The company said the new findings stem from the same incident it disclosed on Oct. 29. Bithumb breach ran for 15 days Bithumb now says an unauthorized outside party accessed the groupware system from 1:49 p.m. on Oct. 12 to 3:22 p.m. on Oct. 27, Korea time, and took personal information and files stored there. That is a sharp change from its first account. Bithumb had said the hack lasted about an hour, from 11:28 a.m. to 12:27 p.m. on Oct. 27, and that it detected the intrusion at 12:14 p.m. that day. The revised timeline means the attacker went unnoticed for more than two weeks. Bithumb first reported that the data of 6,444 customers and 715 employees, or 7,159 people in total, had been exposed. It did not give an updated count on Wednesday. The notice lists customers, employees of partner companies and current and former staff among those affected. Passports, bank accounts and wallet addresses The list of exposed data now runs to 19 items. It includes member numbers, names, mobile numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, resident registration numbers, passport numbers and driver’s license numbers. It also covers bank account numbers, home addresses, gender, nationality, copies of ID documents, occupations, employer names and work contact details, as well as transaction histories and wallet addresses. Bithumb said not every item applies to every person, and that affected users will be told individually by email and text message what was taken. For crypto users, the wallet addresses and transaction records stand out. Paired with names and phone numbers, that kind of data can help scammers target people they know hold digital assets. Bithumb said Daou Office is an internal business system separate from customer exchange accounts and asset data. It said it has found no sign that its exchange service systems or customer database were directly breached, and that it has stepped up real-time monitoring of unusual trades and withdrawals. Bithumb promises compensation The exchange said it blocked the attacker’s IP addresses, fixed the vulnerability behind the incident and is running a security review of all of its externally exposed services. It has also set up a dedicated support desk for victims that covers financial and legal counseling as well as compensation reviews. “We will

item.title: Huawei and crew tout homegrown EDA tools to overcome China’s fab deficit
item.description: Chinese telecom and IT giant Huawei boasted about its advancements in domestic electronic design automation (EDA) software this week, which it needs to accelerate the adoption of homegrown chip manufacturing. EDA is an umbrella term for software, hardware, and services essential to the planning, design, and production of modern chips. Today, Cadence Design Systems, Synopsys, and Siemens dominate the industry, but US export controls have restricted Huawei and other blacklisted Chinese businesses' access to their tools. The US blacklisted Huawei back in 2019 over concerns the telecommunications equipment giant could be forced to inject backdoors into its gear. Unable to access top EDA tools, Huawei’s chip division, HiSilicon, was forced to develop its own with the help of Phlexing Technology. This week, Phlexing chairman Qing He detailed the company’s efforts to bring new EDA tools to support Huawei’s so-called Tau Scaling Law design philosophy. “Tau EDA is the domestic EDA tool chain for Tau chips. It comes from a long, close partnership with Huawei,” he said. We discussed the tech earlier this year, but in a nutshell, it involves using advanced packaging, specifically 3D hybrid bonding, to achieve higher transistor density for a given area. The TSMC of China, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC), is still years behind Taiwan, South Korea, and the US on process technology. It currently has the ability to mass-produce chips on the equivalent of a 7 nm process. For comparison, TSMC began producing 5 nm-class products in 2020 and commenced mass production of 2 nm-class chips in late 2025. So, Huawei aims to use 3D packaging to close the gap, but for this to happen, it first needs tools capable of designing such chips, and that’s just what Phlexing claims to have done with its GloryBolt and GloryEX platforms. “Traditional EDA has long handled only single processes. Tau EDA needs to integrate and decompose multiple processes,” He said. “Coupling multi-scale, multi-structure, and multi-physics issues called for new analysis tools.” This, He says, culminated in the co-development of a process design kit (PDK) with Huawei beginning in 2024. These technologies have now gone live. The development comes as Huawei looks to bring larger, more capable processors to market. We previously discussed the company’s latest developments around AI accelerators, near packaged optics, networking, and rack systems. Many of these advancements will depend on multi-die chip packages, enabled by EDA tools, like those built by Phlexing. ®

item.title: The Fairphone 6 Plus is modular, repairable, and $100 off right now
item.description: The Fairphone 6 Plus comes with 12 replaceable parts. | Photo: Dominic Preston / The Verge Unlike most smartphones, the Fairphone 6 Plus is designed for home repair, with easily replaceable parts that could help extend its lifespan well into the future. That makes its midrange price point easier to justify, especially now that it’s dropped to a new low of $552.49 (about $98 off) at Amazon as part of the retailer’s ongoing Black Friday sale. Fairphone 6 Plus Where to Buy: $649.99 $552.49 at Amazon (black) $649.99 $552.49 at Amazon (green) $649.99 $552.49 at Amazon (blue) The 6.3-inch Fairphone 6 Plus features 12 user-replaceable parts, including the battery, screen, USB-C port, and cameras, all of which you can swap out with the included screwdriver. Replacement parts are relatively affordable, too; a new battery costs $39.99, which helps offset its middling battery life and lack of wireless charging. It also comes with a five-year warranty and up to six Android OS upgrades, making it a good option if you want a phone you can keep using for years. Although repairability is its marquee feature, the 6 Plus is also a solid midrange Android device. Fairphone prioritizes ethically sourced materials , making it a strong choice for environmentally conscious buyers who don’t want to sacrifice performance. Its Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 processor handles everyday tasks well, and its cameras take decent photos, though they’re not quite on par with those of pricier phones. What’s more, it offers a clean, bloatware-free Android experience and modular back panels, which you can swap for optional accessories like a card holder or crossbody strap. Our own Allison Johnson particularly liked the phone’s dedicated switch for turning on customizable focus modes called Moments, which can simplify your homescreen and limit access to distracting apps — something we could all use a little less of. item.title: AI’s stunning progress in maths shows how little we understand it
item.description: MARK SYKES/SPL/Alamy There is a story, possibly apocryphal, that when the mathematician G. H. Hardy was about to undertake a dangerous sea voyage, he sent a postcard to a colleague declaring “I have solved the Riemann hypothesis”. Hardy, a staunch atheist, joked that this would prevent his ship from sinking, as God would never let him claim the credit for such a major result without revealing the details of his proof. Hardy would probably be both astonished and aghast that we now have what seems to be a proof of the Riemann hypothesis , a problem that has vexed mathematicians since the 19th century, but that no one yet understands it. The consensus among mathematicians is that the proof, produced with the aid of AI, will hold, but that it will take much more work to make it comprehensible to humans. However you feel about AI, this is a watershed moment, and one that demonstrates just how little we still understand about the capabilities of the technology. As recently as last month, leading mathematician Terence Tao speculated that AI would eventually solve the Riemann hypothesis, but that it may not happen before 2050. Now, some mathematicians are considering whether their hardest and most infamous remaining problems could be settled within months. In a year that has left mathematicians reeling, this may be the knock-out blow. Advertisement This is a watershed moment, and it shows just how little we understand about AI’s abilities For non-mathematicians, the fall of the Riemann hypothesis is harder to interpret. In the past year, AI has seen incredible advances in both maths and coding, but it is perhaps no coincidence that in these arenas, with nothing more than computer code, answers can swiftly be checked and iterated upon, allowing for rapid improvement. When it comes to other human endeavours though, from art to zoology, such verification is far harder, involving either the messy physical world, or unknowable human taste – or both. Whether this verification gap can be closed may become the biggest question of our age. Answers on a postcard, please.

item.title: Our verdict on Dark Eden by Chris Beckett: ‘Holy cow. Chapter 44!’
item.description: The New Scientist Book Club read Chris Beckett’s Dark Eden in November Since starting the New Scientist Book Club in May 2023, I have aimed to vary our books as much as possible, moving between science fiction and popular science, older classics and the hottest new titles. Occasionally, though, I’m afraid I let the power go to my head and just choose one of my own personal favourites. That’s what I did in November, with Chris Beckett’s novel Dark Eden , a book I’ve loved ever since it won the Arthur C. Clarke award in 2013. Set on the planet Eden, a sunless world that drifts alone far outside the Milky Way, this follows the descendants of two astronauts who were marooned there over a century earlier. Now numbering 532 people, they tell each other stories of the world their ancestors came from, and struggle to survive on this dark, cold planet as they await the return of “one of those sky-boats with lights on them”. I think it is all wildly imaginative and original and exciting. So it was with some trepidation that I awaited the verdict of my fellow book club members on our Discord channel. I really wanted everyone else to love it, too! Free newsletter Sign up to Book Club Sign up to newsletter It started well. “I managed not to stay up all night reading, but the temptation was definitely there – I am hooked,” wrote Dee55. Les was similarly gripped. “Started it? I’ve only gone and finished it, haven’t I? It really got me in, and I found it a fascinating exploration of social anthropology and linguistics in a very small, isolated population. And the world-building was fascinating, too – very different flora and fauna.” Advertisement Several other members also cited the strength of the world-building in Dark Eden . I also love the lanternflowers and woollybucks of this planet, and was fascinated to learn, in an essay Chris wrote for book club members, that, when creating a world for a story, he doesn’t “usually seek to make the whole thing scientifically accurate, but I try to make it hang together in a way that feels coherent”. I think he definitely succeeds in that here. In Dark Eden, I imagined how life might exist on a sunless planet Dark Eden, the November read for the New Scientist Book Club, takes place on a rogue planet outside the Milky Way. Award-winning author Chris Beckett explains how he thought through the science behind this night world There were some excellent debates about the language these people have developed – they double up on words for emphasis, for example (“big big”; “cold cold”), use bastardised forms of our words (“Landing Veekle”; “leckytrickity”), and talk about Starry Swirl – the Milky Way they can see in their skies, a wonderfully evocative image. “I think Beckett has done something really clever here. He’s created a language that feels familiar enough to read naturally, but is sufficiently different to remind us that this is an entirely separate culture that has evolved in isolation,” wrote Maria. “I enjoyed some of

item.title: Is The Time Traveler’s Wife the perfect audiobook to experience on shuffle?
item.description: Josie Ford Feedback is our weekly column of bizarre stories, implausible advertising claims, confusing instructions and more Reader Jenny Ozanne writes to tell us of a horrific incident that befell her partner. He had bought Audrey Niffenegger’s novel The Time Traveler’s Wife as a CD audiobook, to listen to on long car journeys. “After a while, he complained that the plot was completely impossible to follow,” writes Jenny. “It was only when I checked his player that I realized he had accidentally set the CD to ‘shuffle’. “ Advertisement Jenny raises two points, which Feedback heartily endorses: “I’m still not sure what’s more impressive: the story’s ability to survive total chronological chaos, or the fact that he listened to three random chapters before suspecting anything was wrong.” Feedback would suggest that The Time Traveler’s Wife might be the ideal novel to experience on shuffle, since the narrative is heavily non-linear. The main character hops uncontrollably back and forth through history. This led us to wonder: would any similarly chrono-displaced stories survive the experience of being played on shuffle, or even be improved by it? We wondered, for instance, about David Mitchell’s Cloud Atlas . This has six stories set in different periods, including a future in which human clones are used as cheap labour, and a more distant future in which everything has gone a bit Mad Max . The stories are linked by characters in later timelines reading about the earlier ones, and by subtle coincidences. What would it be like on shuffle? However, after careful reflection, we realised there is only one correct answer to this, and that is Shane Carruth’s 2004 film Primer , which tells the story of two tech bros who invent a time machine in their garage. At first, they use it to go back in time and make money on the stock exchange, only to become caught up in an escalating web of betrayal and deception as they endlessly rewrite their lives. Primer is so overcomplicated, so mind-wreckingly confusing, that some poor soul once went so far as to draw a diagram trying to convey its timeline. Posted on Reddit by u/Clawz114, the diagram looks like a cross between a metro map and a flowchart of the inner workings of a chemical factory. It is therefore possible that playing the scenes in random order might actually cause the film to make more sense. The scent of success It’s that time of year when many of us are thinking, “Oh blimey, I need to buy everyone presents” and then having a meltdown when we can’t think of anything. The last refuge of the true gift scoundrel is, of course, the scented candle. This item might as well come with a note saying, “Sorry, I couldn’t think of anything”. Readers looking to step up their scented candle game may wish to investigate JD + Kate Industries , which is run by a pair of humour writers with a sideline in themed scented candles. item.title: ‘Blade Runner 2099’ cast praise the incredible set designs that brought the sci-fi universe to life: ‘it was all so well-realized’ (interview)
item.description: null Prime Video’s " Blade Runner 2099 " has arrived with an 8-episode limited series revealing what the "Blade Runner" world looks like 50 years after the events of director Denis Villeneuve’s "Blade Runner 2049." The most obvious change in this depressing dystopia is that replicants are running the LA show after some unmentionable ecological disaster and humans are now the ones relegated to underclass citizens. Starring Michelle Yeoh as a replicant cop named Olwen whose life clock is running out and Hunter Schafer as Cora, a desperate human posing as a replicant blade runner, "Blade Runner 2099" unties these two in a mystery revolving around a rogue blade runner and a deadly secret that might cause their city to implode. We connected with three of the sci-fi show’s main co-stars, Matthew Needham ("House of the Dragon"), Lewis Gribben ("T2 Trainspotting") and Dimitri Abold ("Love Addicts") to hear more about working with creator/showrunner Silka Louisa, and immersing themselves in " Blade Runner 2099's " vivid futuristic worldbuilding. "For me it's a lot simpler than egos because he's such a goal-oriented person and all of his stuff has such a police procedural quality to it," Needham tells SPACE regarding his role as Yahya, an emotionless replicant who despises all humans. "It was really fun to just follow what Silka [Louisa] did. She wrote this great, really exciting mystery thriller, and I just got to play in that.” Matthew Needham and Hunter Schafer star in "Blade Runner 2099" (Image credit: Amazon Prime Video) Scottish actor Gribben portrays Cora's ailing younger brother Elias, who has compromised mobility and a rocky relationship with his overprotective sister. "I've played a few characters that were fairly vulnerable or insular," he notes. "Then seeing the journey of this character grow in strength and confidence and feel like becoming his own man was so compelling to me. It’s almost a relationship that falls apart between brother and sister, and that's fascinating to me because that’s such a cool dynamic you don’t always really see in television shows. That was quite interesting and made me want to try and be in it." (Image credit: Amazon Prime Video) As Bebeto, a doctor, veteran of the replicants vs. humans war, and a black-market dealer helping his species procure IDs and passports off-world, Abold enjoyed exploring the many facets of his character. "Much like Matthew and Lewis, for me it was the journey that Bebeto goes on," Abold adds. "Starting out as someone who’s so hopeful and has to try and scrape up the last dregs of hope as things start falling apart. Being subject to circumstances like that inherently make for an interesting story arc and story in general. Throwing myself into that, especially after how well Silka crafted the story and script, was something I was totally ready for." item.title: NASA Eyes Crop Candidates for Future Menus
item.description: As NASA prepares for future missions to the Moon and Mars, researchers are studying crops that could provide astronauts with fresh food, nutrition, and variety far from Earth. Such crop variety can help with menus in deep space, something top of mind this week as the nation celebrates Thanksgiving. Strawberries grown in the Space Life Sciences Lab’s controlled environment chamber. Cucumbers are grown in a controlled environment chamber at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Lemon basil is growing in chambers on the International Space Station. NASA Recent testing points to strawberries, cucumbers, and lemon basil as potential options for future explorers. Space crops can absorb carbon dioxide, produce oxygen, and recycle water. These capabilities will become increasingly important as crewed missions extend farther from our home planet. While space crop research advances on Earth, capabilities are also expanding in space. A new investigation from NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division is set to launch to the International Space Station, where the first-of-its-kind prototype growth chamber will provide critical insights for developing crop production systems that could grow crops like these for future Moon Base habitats and Mars missions. Sweet space strawberries Strawberries are among the few sweet fruits under consideration for spaceflight and are nutritious, aromatic, and self-pollinating. Researchers at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida are growing strawberries in flight-like growth chambers to evaluate the potential space crop, and NASA partners at The Australian Research Council Centre for Excellence in Plants for Space also are helping expand knowledge of space strawberries. Researchers at NASA Kennedy, the University of Melbourne, and the University of Western Australia recently tested a wild strawberry against NASA’s leading strawberry candidate, ‘Delizz,’ to see which thrived better under simulated space conditions. Delizz and the wild strawberry produced very different fruits, according to a study published in September in the journal Life Sciences in Space Research. Delizz grew large, red fruit, while the wild strawberry produced small, yellow fruit due to a recessive genetic mutation. But looks are not everything. When grown from a seed, the wild strawberry produced twice as many buds, flowers, and fruit as Delizz. Ultimately, however, NASA’s pick kept its top spot, as the wild strawberry grew too many runners that would take up valuable room aboard a spacecraft. Cucumbers show promise Many crops have been grown in space, but none so far have come from the gourd family. Cucumbers could be the first. Before crops like cucumbers can be grown and eaten in space, they must undergo extensive testing. NASA-funded researchers recently evaluated cucumbers for their growth, yield, and nutrition under spaceflight conditions. item.title: ‘Name National Theatre after Pete Edochie, not Wole Soyinka’ – Brymo to Tinubu
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian singer, Brymo, has urged President Bola Tinubu to name the National Theatre after late veteran actor Pete Edochie instead of Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka, following the death of the Nollywood icon. Brymo made the appeal in a video shared on his official Instagram page on Wednesday, where he paid tribute to Edochie and called on the President to reconsider the naming of the national cultural landmark. “Dear President Tinubu, name the National Theatre after Pete Edochie, not Wole Soyinka, please,” the singer said. He also celebrated the late actor, saying, “Cheers to one of the greatest men, Pete Edochie. May you live forever in our hearts, and on our screens.” Edochie died at the age of 79, with his death announced on Wednesday, November 25, 2026. His passing has prompted tributes from political leaders, colleagues and members of the entertainment industry. President Tinubu, in a tribute, described the late actor as one of Africa’s most recognisable thespians and a pioneer of Nigeria’s film industry. He also recalled Edochie’s portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart in the 1980s. The President praised his performances in productions including Igodo , Rituals and Lionheart , saying his work helped project Nigeria’s cultural heritage and storytelling traditions to audiences around the world. Brymo’s appeal comes against the backdrop of the Federal Government’s decision to rename the National Theatre in Iganmu, Lagos, after Soyinka in 2024, as part of the celebration of the literary icon’s 90th birthday. Tinubu announced that the facility would be known as the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts. The renovated complex was formally commissioned under the new name on October 1, 2025, during Nigeria’s 65th Independence anniversary celebrations. The President had described the renaming as an honour for Soyinka, whose contributions to literature, theatre and human rights advocacy have earned him international recognition, including the 1986 Nobel Prize in Literature. The post ‘Name National Theatre after Pete Edochie, not Wole Soyinka’ – Brymo to Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: DOJ Targets 800 Defendants in Largest-Ever Scam Crackdown, Including Crypto Fraud
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ Targets 800 Defendants in Largest-Ever Scam Crackdown, Including Crypto Fraud The U.S. Justice Department said Tuesday that its largest-ever crackdown on scammers has produced actions against more than 800 defendants since March, with cryptocurrency investment fraud run out of Southeast Asian scam centers among its top targets. The department announced the results of an anti-scam surge that followed President Donald Trump’s Executive Order 14390, signed March 6. Since then, prosecutors have acted in more than 400 cases, bringing new charges, extraditions, guilty verdicts and sentences across 85 federal districts. U.S. agents also helped police in more than 10 countries raid foreign scam call centers and compounds that targeted Americans. Thirty defendants were extradited to face charges in U.S. courts. “Predatory scams against the American people will not be tolerated,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said. “The unprecedented results of this surge are just the beginning.” More than $1 billion in crypto frozen Crypto sits at the center of much of the effort. The State Department said the U.S. and Southeast Asian law enforcement it funds and trains have helped freeze more than $1 billion in stolen cryptocurrency and take down more than 1.4 million fraudulent websites and accounts. The Justice Department’s Scam Center Strike Force, formed in 2025 to go after Southeast Asian crypto fraud, says its crypto seizure team has restrained about $1.08 billion in cryptocurrency from these schemes. The team is focused on returning stolen funds to victims. The FBI’s Operation Blackout has restrained nearly $17 billion in illicit funds, seized more than 14,000 digital devices and helped dismantle more than 29 scam compounds across Asia, Africa and the Middle East, the department said. The FBI also helped free and repatriate more than 2,200 trafficked workers forced to run scams inside those compounds. “The message to these scam syndicates is clear: if you target Americans, justice will find you,” FBI Director Kash Patel said. Scam cases tied to fake crypto platforms In the past month alone, the Criminal Division filed or unsealed charges against more than 30 scam defendants, including those tied to Southeast Asian scam centers running crypto investment fraud schemes. Other cases involved inheritance fraud, jury duty imposters working from Georgia prisons and sweepstakes schemes aimed at elderly Americans. The Secret Service said it has restrained more than $200 million in illicit funds during the surge. One of its cases identified a crypto investment conspiracy run from scam centers in Cambodia that targeted at least 174 U.S. victims. In October, a Chinese national was extradited from the Netherlands and arraigned in California over his alleged role. item.title: FG orders probe as three inmates die after Ilorin jailbreak
item.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The Federal Government has ordered an investigation into the deaths of three condemned inmates at the Oke-Kura Custodial Centre in Ilorin, Kwara State, following a jailbreak attempt last week. The Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, who ordered the investigation, described the deaths as unfortunate and vowed that anyone found culpable would face the full weight of the law. The minister, who visited the facility on Wednesday to assess the situation, also expressed concern that more than 70 condemned inmates at the centre had spent over 10 years on death row, attributing the prolonged stay to delays by state authorities in exercising their powers to grant clemency or commute death sentences. The minister was represented during the visit by the Comptroller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service, Mr Sylvester Nwakuche, who briefed journalists after inspecting the facility. Nwakuche said he returned to Ilorin on the minister’s directive to investigate reports surrounding the incident and assess the condition of the facility. According to him, seven condemned inmates attempted to breach the security of the custodial centre during the jailbreak, but only two succeeded in escaping. He said the remaining five were apprehended and returned to custody, but three subsequently died. “Two succeeded in making their way out of the facility, while the remaining five could not. They were taken back, but unfortunately, we were informed that three out of the five who could not escape lost their lives. “That is an unfortunate incident, and the minister wanted us to come immediately to assess the situation,” he said. The Comptroller-General said a team had been constituted to investigate the deaths, adding that the inquiry would involve clinical, medical and intelligence processes. He assured that the two escaped inmates would be rearrested, regardless of how long it took. Nwakuche also disclosed that more than 70 condemned inmates were being held at the Oke-Kura facility, with some having spent over a decade on death row. He described the situation as a major challenge, noting that the colonial-era facility was accommodating nearly 685 inmates and was severely overcrowded. He said the problem extended beyond Ilorin, disclosing that more than 4,000 inmates were on death row across correctional facilities nationwide. The Comptroller-General appealed to state governors to exercise their constitutional powers by considering the commutation of death sentences to life imprisonment, where appropriate. According to him, such action would enable the Correctional Service to transfer affected inmates to less congested facilities, where they could undergo rehabilitation and vocational training. “We have been appealing to the necessary authorities, the governors, to do what the law permits them to do. Can they commute them into life sentences so that we will be able to distribute them to less congested facilities, where we can also subjec

item.title: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
item.description: In an announcement on Wednesday , the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company's "Starmind" initiative . With several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space , including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency has granted for a full "constellation" of AI satellites. The FCC's approval requires SpaceX to deploy at least one satellite by 2033, and meet the 1 million satellite milestone by 2040. item.title: Pakistani astronaut becomes 1st international visitor to China's Tiangong space station (photos)
item.description: null For the first time ever, a foreign astronaut has set foot inside China's Tiangong space station. That pioneer is Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who arrived at Tiangong aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft early this morning (Nov. 25). "The Chinese space station is always something to look forward to!" the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) wrote in an update today (in Mandarin; translation by Google). "China's 'Tiangong' welcomes partners from all over the world to visit!" Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces, is a payload specialist on Shenzhou-24. He found his way onto the mission thanks to a space-cooperation agreement that China signed with Pakistan in Islamabad in February 2025 . Ali and his two Shenzhou-24 crewmates — commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi — enjoyed a short and smooth ride to their orbital destination. They lifted off atop a Long March 2F rocket on Tuesday (Nov. 24) at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT on Nov. 25) and reached Tiangong a little over six hours later. Tang and Wu will live aboard the outpost for the usual six-month stint. Ali, however, will come home in just a week, hitching a ride with two of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts, who arrived at Tiangong in May . Ali will be busy during his short space stay, conducting a set of joint Chinese-Pakistani experiments. "Four collaborative projects in biotechnology and materials are planned, with Ali also scheduled to conduct an in-orbit experiment involving photosynthetic cyanobacteria," The Times of India wrote today . The third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will remain on the station until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore set a Chinese record, becoming the first astronaut from his country to live in low Earth orbit for a full year. Astronauts from the Soviet Union/Russia and the United States have already blazed this long-duration trail. The global record for longest continuous space stay is 437 days, set by cosmonaut Valeri Polyakov aboard the Mir space station from January 1994 to March 1995. Another look at the Shenzhou-23 and Shenzhou-24 astronauts aboard Tiangong on Nov. 25, 2026. (Image credit: CMSA) Ali is not the first person from Pakistan ever to reach space, by the way. That distinction belongs to adventurer Namira Salim, who traveled to suborbital space on a tourism flight with Virgin Galactic in October 2023. Shenzhou-24 is the 12th crewed mission to Tiangong, a three-module, T-shaped outpost that China finished assembling in late 2022. Well, "finished" might not be the right term; China plans to expand Tiangong , which is currently about 20% as massive as the International Space Station .

item.title: FG Launches ₦1.45trn Lagos Ports Modernisation, Targets 48-Hour Cargo Clearance
item.description: The Federal Government has flagged off the modernisation and upgrade of the Lagos Port Complex, Apapa, and Tin Can Island Port. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, supported by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, and other senior government officials, unveiled the project on Wednesday, describing it as a strategic investment that will reposition Nigeria as a leading maritime hub in Africa and strengthen the country’s competitiveness in global trade. Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony at the Tin-Can Island Port, Oyetola said the project, which would cost £746 million (approximately ₦1.45 trillion), would address decades of infrastructure deficits, reduce logistics costs, attract international shipping lines, stimulate industrial growth and create at least 20,000 direct and indirect jobs. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, said the project, which would cost £746 million (approximately ₦1.45 trillion), would address decades of infrastructure deficits (X/@GboyegaOyetola) He said the modernisation programme was a significant step towards realising President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, which prioritises infrastructure development as a catalyst for economic growth, investment and job creation. According to the minister, the two ports, which have served as major gateways for Nigeria’s international commerce for decades, have become increasingly inadequate to meet the demands of a rapidly expanding economy and changing global shipping requirements. He noted that Apapa Port, established in 1913, was more than a century old, while Tin Can Island Port was commissioned in 1977 when Nigeria’s population stood at approximately 67.2 million, annual trade was about $17 billion, and cargo throughput was 8.11 million metric tonnes. Today, he said, Nigeria’s population has grown to approximately 240 million, merchandise trade exceeds $100 billion annually, while cargo throughput has increased to 129.3 million metric tonnes, nearly 16 times its 1977 level. Oyetola stressed that the mismatch between growing economic activities and ageing port infrastructure had made comprehensive modernisation both urgent and unavoidable. “The cost of inaction is far greater than the cost of modernisation,” he was quoted as saying in a statement by the special adviser to the minister, Bolaji Akinola, as saying, adding that Nigeria will not surrender its competitive advantage. “Our ambition is to attract more direct calls by international shipping lines, retain Nigerian-bound cargo, expand transshipment opportunities and establish our ports as preferred gateways to trade across the African Continental Free Trade Area. We cannot achieve this ambition with infrastructure that falls behind the demands of modern shipping,” the minister said.
