item.title: Entertainment Week Africa 2026 Celebrates Five Years With a Week of Film, Music, Fashion, Tech and Art in Lagos
item.description: The fifth edition of Entertainment Week Africa brought together filmmakers, musicians, designers, artists, tech founders, investors, mentors, policymakers and fans for six days of screenings, showcases, masterclasses and celebrations under the theme Five Years of Closing the Gap . People from 121 countries and territories applied to speak, attend or screen their work, and more than 19,000 people joined the programme in person and online, as EWA streamed its sessions live for the first time. Over the six days, more than 150 speakers led nearly 100 panels, masterclasses, workshops, roundtables and podcast sessions, while around 50 films were screened across the week. The celebrations began on Opening Night at the Livespot Entertarium, where guests were treated to an evening of music, fashion, film and comedy to mark five years of EWA. Sixteen emerging artists performed in front of a room of industry leaders, creatives and partners, and the night featured an exclusive 30-minute screening of University of Side Hustle, the first scripted feature film from Livespot Studios , written by Dami Elebe and executive produced by Deola Art Alade . By day, EbonyLife Place hosted a packed programme across seven tracks: Film & TV; Music; Fashion & Beauty; AI & Tech; Art & Animation; Live Events & Production; and Creative Enterprise. Nissi Ogulu led a masterclass on animation as Africa’s next big storytelling frontier, and From Lagos to Disney explored what it takes to bring African stories to global screens. Creators picked up practical tips in sessions with Victoire, Ifeoma Udeme and Canva. Other sessions tackled sync licensing, music funding, building Africa’s touring circuit and turning creative skills into businesses. The podcast stage kept the energy going with live recordings of CreativiTea and Crea8torium , which closed the final day. Fashion took over the Entertarium for The Runway Coterie, an evening of bold collections that ended with the announcement of the EWA Fashion Lab winners after a week-long programme with mentors. Hooked By Lade won first place with ₦2 million, Estaz took second place and ₦1 million, and Melira placed third, winning ₦500,000. Lush Hair styled the runway as the show’s hair sponsor. Next door, the EWA Art Floor invited guests into The Spaces Between Us , an exhibition that blended photography, painting, installation, archival work, fashion and live performance. Curated by Jumoke Sanwo and produced with Revolving Art Incubator (RAI) as it celebrated its tenth anniversary, the exhibition featured work by 21 Nigerian artists and seven fashion designers. In the EWA Sound Lab, producers and songwriters spent time creating alongside Banx & Ranx, the Grammy-nominated, Juno Award-winning duo whose credits include records for Sean Paul, Dua Lipa and Ella Eyre . item.title: Ladybird browser's first downloadable alpha is surprisingly capable
item.description: After four years of work to build a browser engine from scratch, the Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, offering prebuilt versions for macOS and Linux. Previously, curious users had to compile the browser themselves from its source. Now it's an installable package with automatic updating. Ladybird is most notable for what it isn't: another browser fork. Where Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Opera all run on Google's Blink engine, and Firefox depends on Gecko, Ladybird's rendering engine and its LibJS JavaScript engine were written from scratch. "The engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork," project lead Andreas Kling wrote in Monday's announcement. "The browser around it is modest, but functional." A fourth engine Nearly the entire modern web currently runs on three browser engines. There's WebKit (Safari), Gecko (Firefox), and the biggest of them all, Blink (Chromium). Those limited options mean that web developers often end up optimizing sites for Chromium specifically, since that's where the majority of traffic is, and as a result, the whole web platform tends to follow suit toward whatever the dominant engine supports. item.title: Delta Killings: Reps urge Tinubu to consider emergency measures
item.description: By Gift CmapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has urged President Bola Tinubu to consider invoking constitutional emergency measures in Delta State if escalating political violence degenerates into a breakdown of public order and public safety. The lawmakers also called for a comprehensive investigation into successive attacks on political gatherings across the state, demanding the arrest and prosecution of perpetrators, sponsors and financiers of the violence. The resolutions followed the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by the member representing Okpe/Sapele/Uvwie Federal Constituency, Delta State, Benedict Etanabene, during Wednesday’s plenary. The intervention comes against the backdrop of the November 23 attack on the campaign activities of former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, at Uduere community in Ughelli North Local Government Area, which claimed six lives and left several others injured. Presenting the motion, Etanabene expressed concern over the growing pattern of violence targeting political activities, warning that the attacks were creating an atmosphere of fear among political parties, candidates, supporters and residents. He recalled that violence broke out on November 7 during a political procession along Nnebisi Road, Asaba, resulting in one death and injuries to five persons, according to police figures. He also cited the November 11 attack on a political party’s campaign team at Okpai, Ward 4, Ndokwa East Local Government Area, which reportedly left five members injured. The lawmaker further recalled an incident in September during a political mobilisation exercise in Effurun, Uvwie Local Government Area, where a participant sustained machete injuries and later died in hospital. Etanabene said the latest attack at Uduere, where at least six people were reportedly killed by suspected political thugs, underscored the need for decisive intervention by the Federal Government and security agencies. He warned that the increasing frequency of attacks could trigger a wider breakdown of law and order, undermine peaceful coexistence and threaten the credibility of the 2027 general elections. The lawmaker also expressed concern that the recurrence of violence suggested that existing security arrangements were inadequate to deter perpetrators and protect political actors and innocent citizens. Consequently, the House urged Tinubu, in his capacity as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, to direct relevant security agencies to take immediate steps to prevent further violence and loss of lives in the state. It also urged the Inspector-General of Police to deploy adequate personnel, including tactical and intelligence units, to identified security flashpoints across Delta State. item.title: Hera probe finds DART left a stadium-sized dent in asteroid Dimorphos
item.description: The European Space Agency's Hera probe has revealed a stadium-sized crater on Dimorphos, the asteroid NASA struck with its DART spacecraft in 2022. The Double Asteroid Redirection Test was deliberately crashed into the asteroid on September 26, 2022. The original plan called for a European spacecraft – Asteroid Impact Mission (AIM) – to launch first and observe the before and after effects of DART. AIM was canceled, and the Hera mission launched in 2024. DART was a success. Scientists were able to determine that the impact had indeed changed the orbit of Dimorphos. The question was what else had happened to the asteroid. Scientists spotted ejecta and debris following the DART impact, but the close-up observations by Hera have revealed the full extent of the collision. Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, Director of Research at CNRS / Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur, said: "Scientists debated whether Dimorphos had sustained an impact crater, changed its shape or stayed the same. "Much to our surprise the answer turns out to be all three at once! The face struck by DART has been flattened into an impact crater the size of a sports stadium, which extends across the asteroid's entire width." Scientists also noted that the asteroid is now tumbling in its orbit. Hera is surveying the 151-meter-wide Dimorphos and its larger companion, the 730-meter-wide Didymos, from about 25 to 30 km away. It moves around the pair at roughly 12 cm/s, using thruster firings to trace rectangular paths rather than conventional circular orbits. The plan is to approach closer, to about 13 km, to get higher-resolution snaps. A complicating factor is the discovery that hundreds of orbiting boulders surround the asteroids. Michael Kueppers, ESA's Hera mission scientist, said: "The team will have to take account of these objects in the coming weeks as the mission moves in closer." Hera will deploy two CubeSats, Juventas and Milani, in early 2027. The Italian-led Milani will study surface composition and surrounding dust, while the Luxembourg-led Juventas will use radar to probe Dimorphos's interior before attempting a landing. Scientists also want to measure Dimorphos's mass. Combined with the observed change in its orbit, that will help them assess how effectively DART transferred momentum to the asteroid and improve predictions for future deflection attempts. Hera mission manager Ian Carnelli said: "NASA's DART mission demonstrated that we can change an asteroid's orbit. Hera is now revealing what happened to the asteroid itself. By combining these two missions, humanity is taking a decisive step towards making asteroid deflection a reliable tool for protecting our planet." ®

item.title: Hera spacecraft gets 1st up-close look at stadium-sized hole punched in asteroid by NASA DART mission
item.description: null NASA's DART Earth-defense mission punched a stadium-sized hole in a distant asteroid, and we have seen it up close for the first time thanks to the Hera spacecraft. NASA's DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test) mission made history on Sept. 26, 2022, when it slammed into Dimorphos , the small moonlet of the much larger asteroid Didymos . The mission tested if such an impact could be deployed to divert an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. Scientists have known for some time that this deflection attempt was successful; the system's orbit around the sun was lengthened by 33 minutes, but the European Space Agency's (ESA) Hera mission launched in October 2024 to travel the 120 million miles (194 million kilometers) to the Didymos system to observe the effect of the DART impact in greater detail. Now, the spacecraft has revealed that DART flattened one face of Dimorphos with a stadium-sized crater and set it tumbling chaotically. The impact also appears to have blasted out hundreds of previously unknown boulders that are now circling the binary asteroids. "Scientists debated whether Dimorphos had sustained an impact crater, changed its shape, or stayed the same," Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, Director of Research at the Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur, said in a statement. "Much to our surprise, the answer turns out to be all three at once! The face struck by DART has been flattened into an impact crater the size of a sports stadium, which extends across the asteroid's entire width." An important step for Earth defence Michael Kueppers, ESA's Hera mission scientist, detailed some of the changes to the impacted moonlet seen by the spacecraft: "As Hera returned more images, it became clear that the DART impact has left Dimorphos tumbling wildly in its orbit. "Another big surprise is that Hera is showing that the asteroids are surrounded by hundreds of orbiting boulders, just a few meters in size." It wasn't all change for Dimorphos. Hera discovered that the boulder fields covering the regions of the moonlet not impacted look just like they did when DART imaged it in 2022. (Left) Didymos system seen by DART in 2022 (Right): the same system seen by Hera in 2026 (Image credit: ESA/NASA) Hera isn't finished with Didymos and its moonlet. The ESA spacecraft is currently in a rectangular orbit around the asteroid binary system, using its thrusters to maintain a distance of around 18.6 miles (30 kilometers). This allows Hera to continue observing Didymos and Dimorphos. Hera will soon come to within around 8 miles (13 km) of the asteroids, capturing even more detailed images of the space rocks. Following this, it will deploy two showbox-sized CubeSats , which will get even closer to the asteroids. The CubeSat Juventas will use low-frequency radar to probe the interior of Dimorphos, the first time this has ever been done for an asteroid, and will eventually attempt to land on the moonlet to measure its gravity. item.title: Tinubu’s govt has made everyone poor — Obi
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of worsening poverty in the country, saying Nigerians should not continue to endure the hardship. Obi said his proposed government with former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso would prioritise job creation, production, poverty reduction and the responsible management of public resources. He spoke on Wednesday at the NDC town hall meeting in Edo State, where he urged Nigerians to support the party in the 2027 general election. “Tinubu has put everybody into poverty; that poverty must not continue,” Obi said. The former Anambra State governor said his ambition was to move Nigeria away from a consumption-driven economy towards one focused on production, arguing that such a shift would create jobs and improve living conditions. “We want to build a new Nigeria that is possible. We want to remove Nigeria from consumption to production so all of you can have jobs. We want to pull Nigerians out of poverty, we want to build a country that cares for everybody,” he said. Obi also promised to tackle corruption and ensure that public resources were deployed for the benefit of citizens. “We want to build a country, where people will no longer steal public money. Public money must be used for public good. That’s what we want to do,” he said. Calling on supporters to remain vigilant during the 2027 elections, the NDC candidate urged voters to stay at their polling units after casting their ballots until the votes were counted. He said the party would not want its votes compromised through electoral malpractice. “We want you to go out in 2027, you’re our polling agents. When you vote, don’t go home. Stay there until your vote is counted. We don’t want them to rig us out. We must get it right this time because we want to build a better society,” Obi said. He urged Nigerians to vote for him and Kwankwaso, saying their proposed administration would be led by people committed to serving the country. “Vote Kwankwaso and I to start that new Nigeria. We want to make sure that we have a government of people, who have compassion, who have commitment, who have the energy to do the job,” he added. Obi further pledged to build a society where opportunities would not depend on personal connections or family background. “We want to build a society where a child of nobody can be somebody without knowing anybody,” he said. The post Tinubu’s govt has made everyone poor — Obi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: HRF Announces Funding of Seven Bitcoin Projects for People Living Under Authoritarian Regimes
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine HRF Announces Funding of Seven Bitcoin Projects for People Living Under Authoritarian Regimes The Human Rights Foundation (HRF) is pleased to announce grants from its Bitcoin Development Fund for seven projects advancing bitcoin self-custody, financial privacy, and education for people living under authoritarian regimes. One project translates bitcoin terminology into 21 African languages. Another mines bitcoin with surplus solar power in rural Nigerian homes, paying it directly to the households that generate it. Others build tools for people facing repression anywhere — activists who need to find and fix the privacy leaks in their bitcoin use, communities who need self-custody devices built from parts found in any electronics store, observers who need election evidence preserved before it disappears, and people who need to turn an ordinary phone into an offline Bitcoin wallet. Together, these efforts help human rights defenders, journalists, nonprofits, and individuals hold, send, and verify their money freely under repression. HRF’s grantees for Round III of 2026 are: CryoBrick Many people want to self-custody bitcoin, but in much of the world, buying a hardware wallet is too expensive. CryoBrick transforms feature phones into offline Bitcoin signing devices. Because it looks and works like an ordinary phone, activists living under authoritarian regimes can self-custody bitcoin while maintaining plausible deniability. Technical Director Apalok will use HRF’s support to conduct comprehensive security hardening and peer review, integrate Bitchat for offline messaging, and publish how-to guides, expanding access to bitcoin and the property rights it protects to a far larger global user base. Exonumia Africa: Bitcoin Glossary Bitcoin’s benefits remain out of reach for many African communities because high-quality education resources do not exist in their local languages. Exonumia , an open-source project that translates Bitcoin educational content, is building a Bitcoin Glossary in 21 African languages. The project will coordinate a continent-wide community of translators through three in-person and 12 virtual translation sprints, where native speakers review and validate more than 250 terms. Because every term is validated by native speakers rather than machines, the approved terms give wallet developers a trustworthy foundation for localizing bitcoin software into African languages, extending access to bitcoin education and the financial freedom it offers. HRF’s support will see the glossary published as a free public resource. Pawavox In much of Africa, democratic elections remain a struggle and most countries are not fully free. Exacerbating this, evidence of fraud documented by citizens is often lost because paper forms go missing and photos and messages cannot be verified. item.title: Bandits abduct six in midnight raid on Kaduna community
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Suspected bandits have abducted six residents during a midnight attack on Mama G area, near MPH, Millennium City, in Chikun Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The attackers reportedly stormed two houses around 11:30pm on Tuesday, shooting sporadically and initially abducting nine persons. However, three of the victims, including an elderly woman, a mother and her toddler, were later released, leaving six others in the custody of the abductors. The incident has heightened fears among residents of Millennium City, who say repeated attacks have made life increasingly difficult, forcing some homeowners and tenants to abandon their houses over fears of kidnapping. One of the residents, whose wife was among those abducted, was seen weeping as he appealed for help to secure her release. He expressed concern about her health, saying she had difficulty walking before the incident. “I don’t know her condition as we speak because she is having problems walking, and now they have taken her away. I’m appealing to whoever can help me rescue her from them,” he said. Another resident, Hassan Salihu, said residents heard gunshots around 11:30pm on Tuesday and immediately contacted one another to establish where the shooting was taking place. “When we heard gunshots, we started communicating with other residents to know the exact location. We later discovered it was here in our community. “We alerted the soldiers, and they came through Keke A and remained here until 4am, but we didn’t see the abductors leaving the area,” he said. Salihu appealed to the Kaduna State Government and security authorities to establish a military outpost in the community, particularly along routes allegedly used by the attackers. Similarly, Adamu Muhammad Maina said the attack threw residents into confusion, adding that nine people were initially taken from two neighbouring houses. “It was a terrible situation. Nine people were initially abducted from our neighbours’ houses. Four people were abducted from one house, including a woman and her toddler, but they were released,” he said. He explained that five other residents were taken from the second house, including an elderly woman who was subsequently released because of her inability to walk. “Now we have six people with the bandits, and nobody knows their location,” he added. A female resident, who pleaded anonymity, said the persistent attacks had traumatised the community, forcing some landlords and tenants to abandon their homes. “We are traumatised because most house owners are now abandoning their houses. We find it difficult to sleep inside our homes, so we are pleading with the relevant agencies, including the state and Federal Governments, to come to our aid,” she said. Residents also disclosed that suspected bandits had attempted to invade the community on Monday night but were repelled by security operatives before returning on Tuesday night. item.title: Southern Nigeria deserves eight years in presidency like North — Shehu Sani
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo Former Kaduna Central Senator, Shehu Sani, has said Southern Nigeria deserves to retain the Presidency for eight years, just as the North did under the All Progressives Congress (APC), in the interest of fairness, equity and justice. Sani said individual political ambitions should not be allowed to undermine the historical relationship, solidarity and common interests shared by the North and South. He spoke on Wednesday while delivering the second-term inauguration lecture of Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, in Osogbo. The former lawmaker said the principle of power rotation should be respected to ensure fairness between the two regions. “Like every other part of the country, the South deserves respect for the principle of political power rotation. Power has been held in the North for eight years. It should be allowed, in the spirit of fairness, equity and justice, to be in the South for eight years. “I am not saying this because I am in Osun State or because His Excellency is my friend or brother. Everyone who knows my history and has followed my public statements wherever I have spoken knows that this has always been my position. “The political ambitions of individuals should not be allowed to disrupt the good relationship, historical connections, commonality and solidarity that exist between the North and the South. We must not throw these values into the gutter because of the ambitions of individuals,” he said. Speaking on the theme, “Beyond the Ballot Box: Subnational Governance, Institutional Independence and the Future of Democracy in Nigeria,” Sani urged Adeleke to make his second term a period of institutional reforms, economic transformation and measurable development. He described the governor’s renewed mandate as a social contract that comes with greater expectations and responsibilities. item.title: Police arrest three suspects over political violence in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has arrested three suspects over alleged political violence during a political gathering in Zauro, Makera and surrounding communities in Birnin Kebbi Local Government Area. The arrests followed reports of violence and the alleged presence of individuals wielding dangerous weapons during political activities organised by members of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday, saying preliminary investigations revealed that the gathering, reportedly presented as a distribution of relief materials, was organised by the wife of the ADC governorship candidate. According to him, the activities took place in Zauro, Makera, Gwadangwaji, Gawasu, Morida and Karyo without prior notification to the Police at least 48 hours before their commencement. Usman said the failure to notify the Police violated an agreement reached between the Command and political parties during a stakeholders’ engagement on September 7, 2026, as well as a subsequent meeting with the party’s caucus on November 2, 2026. He explained that during the meetings, the party had undertaken to notify the Commissioner of Police of all political activities at least 48 hours ahead to enable adequate security arrangements. The police spokesperson said video evidence obtained by the Command showed individuals in the convoy carrying sticks, machetes and swords, while some speakers allegedly made inciting statements capable of disrupting public peace. He added that some vehicles in the convoy were observed without registration numbers or with questionable number plates, while sirens were also used in violation of applicable traffic regulations. Usman said the Command condemned the conduct, warning that political activities must not degenerate into thuggery, violence or inflammatory statements. He said the Police would not tolerate any action capable of undermining public peace or setting a dangerous precedent ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Command urged the party’s leadership to honour its commitment to peaceful political engagement and cooperate with security agencies, including handing over individuals involved in unlawful conduct. Usman said the three suspects had been charged to court for prosecution, adding that any breach of agreed security protocols or applicable laws would be dealt with accordingly. The Command also called on relevant authorities to investigate reports of minors’ involvement in political activities and take appropriate measures to protect them from exploitation, violence and other harmful circumstances. In a related development, the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) in Jega reported another political activity organised by the same party without prior notification to the Police. The organisers were subsequently directed to reschedule the rally and formally notify the Police to enab

item.title: CleanSpark Weighs Selling More Bitcoin Than It Mines After $987M Loss
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine CleanSpark Weighs Selling More Bitcoin Than It Mines After $987M Loss CleanSpark (Nasdaq: CLSK) may sell more bitcoin than it mines as it works to lower risk on its balance sheet, President and CFO Gary Vecchiarelli said Tuesday, after the miner posted a $987.1 million net loss for its fiscal year ended Sept. 30, as lower bitcoin prices hit the value of its holdings. “We see the selling of a small amount of bitcoin in excess of the quarterly production to be one way of derisking,” Vecchiarelli said on the company’s earnings call. He added that CleanSpark will be “very reactionary to markets” and use that cash to avoid dilution or new debt. Vecchiarelli said CleanSpark already aims to sell virtually all of the bitcoin it mines to run the business, and that it has sold some bitcoin since year-end to build cash for acquisitions it expects to make soon. “It is reasonable to expect that we will fund highly accretive acquisitions and development of projects by selling or borrowing against our bitcoin,” he said. Bitcoin swings drove the loss The Las Vegas-based company reported full-year revenue of $576.5 million, down 25%. The loss came to $3.74 per basic share, and adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $304.2 million. Vecchiarelli said about two-thirds of the swing from last year’s $364 million profit came from noncash mark-to-market losses on bitcoin. CleanSpark recorded a $281.6 million loss on the fair value of its bitcoin for the year, versus a $425.6 million gain a year earlier. It also took $177.1 million in impairment charges, mostly tied to turning its Sandersville, Georgia, mining site into a data center. Bitcoin ended the fiscal year near $83,600, down from about $114,000, the CFO said. The fourth quarter looked different. CleanSpark earned $9.8 million, or 4 cents a share, helped by a $305.6 million gain on its bitcoin, even as revenue dropped 46% from a year earlier to $120.9 million. Analysts had expected a loss of 33 cents a share and revenue of about $134.3 million, Investing.com reported . The miner produced 7,253 BTC during the year, down 8% as network difficulty rose and it curtailed some machines, and ended September with about 200,000 machines running, down from 225,000 at the end of June. That cut lifted fleet efficiency to 14.8 joules per terahash, while average hashrate fell to 36.0 EH/s. CleanSpark held 13,530 BTC, including pledged collateral, at the end of September, worth about $1.1 billion then. Its annual report shows it sold 1,532 bitcoin during the year and used another 6,068 to settle derivatives. At Wednesday’s price near $57,700, 13,530 BTC would be worth roughly $780 million. CleanSpark shares hit a new low CleanSpark stock fell to a new 52-week low of $4.43 shortly after Wednesday’s open, before trimming losses to about $4.85 around 10 a.m. ET, down roughly 5% from Tuesday’s $5.12 close, as the Nasdaq sank about 4% at the open. item.title: Microsoft's NTLM security changes trip up third-party logins
item.description: Microsoft's November security updates can break authentication in some third-party applications and devices following changes to NTLM message signing. Affected systems include authentication proxy servers, single sign-on (SSO) products, and application packaging tools, the company's support notice says. The failures stem from products that claim to supply required information during NTLM authentication but return incomplete or empty data, Microsoft said: "An affected device might set the NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_TARGET_INFO flag in its CHALLENGE_MESSAGE but provide an empty or incomplete TargetInfo field." Administrators can use the notice's network trace and event log examples to identify affected products. For confirmed cases, the temporary workaround is to set the ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm Registry value to 1 on affected clients. This stops the client offering signing, backing out the new default rather than fixing the incompatible product. The recommended long-term options are a vendor update or Kerberos authentication, where supported. The value sits under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 and defaults to 0, enabling clients to offer signing on non-anonymous connections. The NTLM changes arrived in the November 10 update as phase 1 in a 2-phase process. In phase 1, "Windows client devices begin offering NTLM signing on all connections by default. Servers accept both signed and unsigned clients. Auditing events identify clients not using signing." Phase 2, scheduled for May 2027, will make Windows servers require NTLM signing by default. "Clients that do not offer signing will be rejected by secure servers," Microsoft stated. Ominously, Microsoft warned that it "might remove the registry keys at a future date," so the company is not kidding about the temporary workaround thing. The additional protections were added to address CVE-2026-118737 , a vulnerability in which "improper verification of cryptographic signature in Windows Remote Procedure Call Runtime allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network." NTLM is on Microsoft's hit list, having joined the Deprecated Features list in 2024. It dates back to the era of Windows NT, and Microsoft has made clear that it wants customers to move to Kerberos, which became the default in 2000. Even so, NTLM lingers on. Deprecation doesn't remove Microsoft's obligation to secure NTLM while it remains in supported Windows releases. For administrators, though, the immediate task is identifying incompatible products before temporary exceptions give way to stricter enforcement. ®

item.title: ‘I’m done with Rivers, FCT; give me Imo, Kwara to deliver’ – Wike tells Tinubu
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has asked President Bola Tinubu and the Director General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, to assign him Imo and Kwara states, saying he has completed his political mobilisation work in Rivers State and the Federal Capital Territory. Wike made the request during a town hall meeting with residents and members of the Rainbow Coalition in Gokana Local Government Area of Rivers State. The minister said he had been assigned to coordinate Rivers and the FCT but was now seeking two additional states to work on ahead of the next election. “I was assigned to coordinate Rivers State and the FCT. Frankly speaking, I am done with these states, and we have no work to do again,” he said. Wike said he wanted the President and the campaign director general to give him more responsibilities, adding that he was willing to take charge of Imo State because of what he described as political challenges in the state. “As I am going now, I will plead with the Campaign DG and President Tinubu to add two more states for me to deliver. It’s a serious matter,” he said. He also referred to reports of divisions within the political structure in Kwara State, saying he would like to take responsibility for delivering the state for Tinubu. “From what I am told, they are having some problems in Imo State. So, I will like to go there and deliver Imo for Mr President,” Wike said. “Secondly, I have not confirmed, but what I read on social media is that there are some divisions in Kwara. So, I plead with the DG of the APC Presidential Council, Senator Yari, and Mr President to allow me to take over Imo and Kwara States, because I am done with Rivers and FCT,” he added. Wike’s remarks signal his willingness to take on a wider political mobilisation role in support of Tinubu, although he acknowledged that his information about the alleged divisions in Kwara was based on social media reports and had not been independently confirmed. item.title: Childhood, Career Come Full Circle for Budget Analyst at NASA Goddard
item.description: Conversations about NASA were the norm around the dinner table during Ashley Knight’s childhood. Her parents worked at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, and discussions about happenings at the agency continued even when they came home from the office. “I remember a poignant dialogue we had after the space shuttle Challenger disaster,” Knight recalled. “However, we talked just as much about the engaging work my parents were doing inside Goddard’s gates.” Her father Lyle Knight was a mechanical engineer, while her mother Julia Knight worked the bulk of her career in human resources. They brought their daughter on center for Take Your Child to Work Day and other events, and over time she became hooked. “I saw the chambers where spacecraft and instruments were being tested, as well as other facilities used to help further space exploration. Above all, I witnessed the passion and collaborative spirit everyone had at Goddard,” Knight said. “As a child, I found it incredibly fascinating.” Ashley Knight (right) on a visit to NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Md., while her parents were employees. Photo courtesy of Ashley Knight It all came full circle in late August when, after growing up around NASA and later working several contractor roles for the agency, Knight and a number of her colleagues in the Goddard Office of the Chief Financial Officer were sworn in as federal employees as part of a workforce directive to strengthen the agency’s technical core competencies by bringing mission-critical positions into the civil service. She began her Goddard career more than two decades ago following graduation from the University of Maryland in nearby College Park. As the job search began after commencement, one organization inevitably stood out, along with one particular mission. When she came across a contractor job opening at Goddard in support of the Hubble Space Telescope team, Knight jumped at the opportunity. “Hubble was doing amazing things, and I always admired how they fixed the faulty mirror,” she said, referring to how astronauts and team members corrected an early spherical aberration during the observatory’s first servicing mission. “It was exciting to become involved with such a flagship mission, especially coming right out of college.” As a project support analyst, Knight assisted engineers with test plans, data gathering, and hardware procurement for Hubble’s fifth and final shuttle servicing mission. Knight stands in front of space shuttle Atlantis, which was used for the Hubble Space Telescope’s fifth and final shuttle servicing mission, while she was a project support analyst for the Hubble team. Photo courtesy of Ashley Knight Following the mission’s completion in 2009 and subsequent end of the Hubble shuttle servicing era, she took on a similar role with the Robotic Refueling Mission in what was then the Satellite Servicing Capabilities Office at Goddard – now known as NASA’s In-Space Servicing, Ass

item.title: Ars Live recap: Don’t expect military attacks on data centers to stop
item.description: Drone attacks on data centers. Amazon data centers came under military attack for the first time ever in the Middle East this year, and Russia and Ukraine exchanged an unprecedented flurry of drone strikes on each other’s data centers. To examine what such attacks on data centers mean for the future of cloud services that all modern societies depend upon, Ars hosted a live discussion. In a conversation with Ars Technica Tech Reporter Jeremy Hsu, Joseph Jarnecki at the Royal United Services Institute first talked about why public cloud data centers have increasingly become military targets during the 2026 Iran war and the ongoing full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine: We see an increasing acknowledgement and fact of dual use in particularly the public cloud, but also just across the board in private cloud data centers as well. The dual use that I refer to is the utilization of compute functions within these data centers—within cloud services—by militaries, for example, to run battlefield management systems, to do their HR, to do their resource management. Once a military uses a piece of civilian infrastructure, at least under international law or in terms of the principles of targeting that are taken forward by militaries, it can sometimes become a military object and is therefore of interest to an adversary, and there's an incentive to target it. Jarnecki also highlighted the fact that relatively cheap kamikaze drones can inflict disproportionate economic costs and create widespread cloud disruptions when striking data centers: Read full article Comments

item.title: US Treasury financial crimes unit becomes latest fed breach victim
item.description: The US Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) has taken some systems offline following unauthorized access, disrupting regulatory filings for financial institutions. An alert has gone up on FinCEN's Bank Secrecy Act E-Filing website, as shown in this archived copy , informing those who need to submit reports that they might not be able to while the agency deals with the situation. FinCEN not only enforces compliance with the Bank Secrecy Act and associated regulations but also collects and analyzes financial intelligence for sharing with other US agencies and foreign government partners. In other words, it has some juicy info in its databases. “FinCEN is investigating a cybersecurity incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems,” the alert states. “As a proactive measure, FinCEN has taken some systems offline.” FinCEN hasn't said which systems intruders accessed, but clues in the deadline extension notice the agency posted alongside the warning suggest the disruption affects its reporting services for banks and other financial institutions required to submit reports detailing certain financial transactions and suspicious activity that may indicate money laundering or other illicit activity. FinCEN's Secure Data Transfer Mode, one method of submitting those reports, appears to be affected, as do services companies use to submit beneficial ownership information reports and individuals use to update their FinCEN identifiers. Eligible organizations and individuals with filings or updates due from November 18 through December 29 now have until December 30 to submit them. The Register has learned that there’s no evidence of any unauthorized access to Bank Secrecy Act data or beneficial ownership databases. That said, the investigation is ongoing - so that could change. “Treasury is working with the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, and third-party forensic examiners to determine the scope and impact of the incident,” a FinCEN official told us in an email. Several US government agencies have experienced cybersecurity incidents in recent months, including the ATF and the FBI , and reports emerged this week that intruders had also compromised an unclassified CIA system . While US authorities have linked previous cyberespionage campaigns to Chinese or other government-backed groups , financially motivated criminal groups have also targeted federal agencies. As the FinCEN breach is still under investigation, the agency hasn’t stated who may be involved and for what purpose. ®

item.title: NASA sends planes to monitor US Army's lead detonation. 'Irresponsible' to compare it to Chernobyl, agency chief says
item.description: null NASA has sent three different research aircraft and is using a satellite-based instrument to support the U.S. Army's detonation of degraded explosives at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, the agency announced yesterday (Nov. 24). After a week-long delay caused by public concern over the event creating clouds of lead and toxic materials, today (Nov. 25) around 10 a.m. EDT (1400 GMT) the U.S. Army has planned to execute a controlled detonation of five tons of aging explosives at the ammunition plant. The detonation follows concerns that cooling winter temperatures or attempts to chemically neutralize the materials could lead to an unexpected, uncontrolled explosion. "In challenging circumstances such as this, you want the nation's best on the field. That is precisely why you call on NASA , putting our airborne and space-based sensors and some of the brightest scientific minds in the country to work," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in an online statement . To support this detonation, NASA deployed three research aircraft : a P-3 Orion, a Gulfstream III from NASA's Langley Research Center and a B200 from NASA Ames. The agency is also monitoring the situation using its TEMPO (Tropospheric Emissions: Monitoring of Pollution) instrument which is mounted and orbiting Earth on a commercial satellite. "Working alongside our partners across the federal government, NASA is utilizing its advanced scientific instruments and expertise to collect environmental and atmospheric data to inform the broader federal response," NASA stated . The environmental monitoring using TEMPO is especially important as the materials to be detonated include lead azide and other toxic components that are causing not just environmental worries, but significant local concern over possible health repercussions. This concern is severe enough that, following detonation, officials are encouraging local residents to stay indoors with the doors and windows closed for 24-28 hours. In fact, the CDC has activated an emergency response "to provide accurate public health communication and technical assistance," the CDC stated online . They have also offered additional guidance for locals to try and mitigate as much exposure to toxic materials like lead dust as possible. In the map below, which comes from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers using satellite data, the highlighted area shows where surface deposits of lead is expected to exceed the maximum allowable amounts on surfaces per the Environmental Protection Agency. In this map in the area surrounding the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, the highlighted area shows where surface deposits of lead is expected to exceed the maximum allowable amounts on surfaces per the Environmental Protection Agency. item.title: Eye of the Sahara
item.description: NASA/Luke Delaney The Richat Structure, also known as the “Eye of the Sahara,” is seen from the International Space Station as it orbited above on Nov. 14, 2026. It is an eroded geological dome about 100 million years old created by igneous activity and uplift in the nation of Mauritania. In this type of geologic structure, rocks exposed in the center of the “bullseye” are older than rocks forming the outer rings. This structure measures 45 kilometers (28 miles) across and is made up of igneous and sedimentary rocks. Image credit: NASA/Luke Delaney

item.title: Lead azide detonation sends clouds over Iowa as questions of health risks swirl
item.description: In a powerful explosion that launched gray-white clouds over southeastern Iowa, the Army detonated 68 barrels containing 9,700 pounds (4.4 tons) of degraded lead azide on Wednesday at about 9 am CT, preventing a spontaneous unmitigated explosion of the crystallized, highly unstable compound. The detonation occurred at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa, a town of fewer than 400 people. Residents within a 5-mile area of the facility were advised to evacuate, while people farther out were told to shelter in place, close windows and doors tightly, turn off fans, and set indoor air systems to recirculate. Local Iowa outlet KWQC caught the plume from the two earth-covered containers, which were detonated simultaneously. A KWQZ journalist, at a reportedly safe distance from the blast, said on the live broadcast that he could see and then feel the shockwave roll through the crop field in which he was standing. item.title: Next Technology (NXTT) Sells 500 Bitcoin to Fund AI Push
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Next Technology (NXTT) Sells 500 Bitcoin to Fund AI Push Next Technology Holding (Nasdaq: NXTT) sold about 500 bitcoin last week and said it will put the money toward artificial intelligence projects, the latest public company to trim its bitcoin treasury as prices slide. The Japan-based software firm disclosed in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday that it sold the coins on Nov. 21 for about $29.22 million. That works out to an average price of $58,468.11 per bitcoin, net of fees and expenses. The sale leaves NXTT with 5,333 BTC. The company was paid in tether (USDT), the dollar-pegged stablecoin, rather than in dollars. NXTT said it plans to use the proceeds for research and development of its AI-related initiatives, including its AI software products and services, as well as for general corporate purposes. A shift away from buying The sale is the first under a program the company’s board approved on Oct. 30. That program allows NXTT to sell or pledge its bitcoin “from time to time in one or more tranches,” through exchange sales, block trades or loans that use the coins as collateral, with the stated aim of “reducing risk exposure and enhancing liquidity.” The filing also repeats a line from the company’s latest quarterly report that marks a clear break from its earlier approach. NXTT “does not currently expect to purchase additional Bitcoin,” the company said, adding that it has adjusted its strategy to focus on managing the coins it already holds. The program has no expiration date and doesn’t require the company to sell any set amount. The board can change, pause or end it at any time. As of Nov. 24, NXTT said it had not pledged any of its bitcoin as collateral. How NXTT built its stack NXTT, which is incorporated in Wyoming but based in Saitama Prefecture, Japan, describes itself as running two strategies: AI-enabled software development and holding bitcoin. It keeps substantially all of its coins with Japan-based institutional custodians, according to its quarterly filing . The company held 833 BTC at the end of 2024 and added 5,000 BTC in 2025, bringing its total to 5,833 BTC. Its filing puts the cost basis of those coins at about $183.1 million, or roughly $31,400 per bitcoin, meaning last week’s sale still came in well above what the company paid on average. Falling prices have still hit the books. NXTT reported a net loss of $32.2 million for the first nine months of 2026, compared with net income of $295.1 million a year earlier. The company said the swing came mainly from a drop in the fair value of its digital assets. The company has also been reshaping its leadership around AI. Earlier this month it named Chan Phang Chuen, a former platform architect focused on computing infrastructure and AI inference, as chief technical officer after Hongliang Liu resigned from the role. Treasury firms turn sellers NXTT joins a growing list of public companies selling bitcoin to fund other businesses.

item.title: NASA's nuclear-powered Mars delivery service takes shape
item.description: NASA has settled key design choices for its planned nuclear-fission-powered spacecraft, Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, following a mission review in October. Targeting launch in late 2028, SR-1 would be the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth orbit. It is designed to demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion and deliver a capsule carrying three helicopters to Mars. There have been some changes since NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman showed off the concept [PDF] at the agency's Ignition event in March. Improved shielding and spacecraft design will allow a shorter boom between the reactor and the spacecraft's main body, protecting its electronics and the SkyFall payload. The shorter boom will, according to NASA, "reduce weight, simplify assembly, and help streamline the spacecraft’s design." The revised design also includes larger X-band antenna dishes to transmit data to Earth. Decisions are still pending on how many radiator panels the vehicle needs, the output power levels of the nuclear power module, and how long the reactor will operate. Currently, the mission calls for the spacecraft to start its reactor once it has left Earth orbit and gradually ramp up power. After a period during which performance data will be sent back to Earth, the reactor will be shut down until after the SkyFall capsule, containing a trio of Mars Ingenuity-class helicopters, is delivered to Martian orbit. Solar arrays will power the spacecraft during its cruise to Mars. The fission reactor will then be reactivated to let engineers collect more data on its performance in deep space. NASA also awarded a $39.3 million contract to Johns Hopkins University's Applied Physics Laboratory to develop the heat rejection system for the nuclear power module. "Further maturation of the spacecraft plans will focus on reducing risk, simplifying the design, and staying on schedule," the agency said. The latter part regarding the schedule is certainly a challenge . Meeting the late-2028 launch target leaves roughly two years to finish designing, building, and testing the spacecraft. ESA is also targeting late 2028 for its long-delayed Rosalind Franklin rover. Missing the intended Mars departure opportunity could push SR-1 into a later launch window, although NASA has not specified a fallback schedule. ®

item.title: Satellites watch volcanic eruptions add new beaches on Iwo Jima | Space photo of the day for Nov. 25, 2026
item.description: null Iwo Jima on Oct. 26, 2026 on the left and the same location on Nov. 11, 2026 shows the impact of a volcanic eruption. (Image credit: NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey ) Iwo Jima looks remarkably different from space after a volcanic eruption created new land extending the Japanese island's beaches. What is it? On Oct. 27, Japan's Meteorological Agency detected an underwater volcanic eruption off the shores of Iwo Jima. Soon after this initial detection of the "submarine" volcano, satellites orbiting our planet started taking a look, observing to see what havoc this eruption might wreak. When you compare the satellite images above captured by the Landsat 9 satellite's Operational Land Imager (OLI), you can see the stark differences between the island on October 26 before the eruption and weeks later on November 11. The island was also observed by NASA's NISAR spacecraft as well as the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensors. Together, this imagery gave researchers a more complete picture of how the eruption continued and the effects it left behind. And amazingly, with satellite imagery experts have been able to show that the eruption has actually added more land to the island's beaches. Why is it incredible? On Nov. 16, Japan's Coast Guard confirmed in a statement that about 125 acres (50 hectares) of new land is now connected to the island's southeast beach following the recent volcanic eruption. This is not the first time that a volcano has created new land. Lava and ash from a volcanic eruption can solidify and accumulate, adding land material around the volcano or to a nearby coast if it is located offshore or underwater, as we saw in this case. But these new landforms aren't always permanent fixtures. This new addition to the island's beach could easily and quickly be washed away by the waves, which happened on Iwo Jima just a few years ago in 2023 . And experts expect the same thing to happen with this new land. "I imagine we'll see this new land wash away within a few months," Daniel Slayback, a scientist at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center who has previously studied landforms created by volcanic eruptions, said in a statement . "But we'll have to wait and see."

Credits: NASA, ESA, and S. Terry (University of Maryland); Image Processing: G. Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) An expanse of stars gleams in a rainbow of colors in these NASA Hubble Space Telescope images of the Milky Way. The images focus on an area of sky toward the galactic bulge, a densely packed, spherical region of stars that surrounds the center of a galaxy’s disk. These Hubble observations are part of a survey that will help researchers better interpret upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope observations as they seek to characterize the stars and search for exoplanets in this busy region of our galaxy. Astronomers study the Milky Way’s galactic bulge because it holds nearly a quarter of the galaxy’s stellar mass, and its proximity allows them to examine the region in greater detail. Although we can see the glow from these crowded spheres of stars in other galaxies, they are too jam-packed and far away to resolve individual stars. By studying the Milky Way’s galactic bulge, researchers hope to find new planets and better understand how galaxies form, evolve, and interact over billions of years. Teeming with stars in a rainbow of colors, this NASA Hubble Space Telescope image will help researchers interpret future Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope data of the same region. NASA, ESA, and S. Terry (University of Maryland); Image Processing: G. Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) Hubble views the universe primarily in ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared light, while Roman collects data in near-infrared light and some visible light. item.title: Bitcoin Price Slumps Below $57,500 as Nasdaq Sinks 4% at Open
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Slumps Below $57,500 as Nasdaq Sinks 4% at Open The bitcoin price fell to near $57,500 on Wednesday morning, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data, as Wall Street opened sharply lower on a deepening technology selloff, hotter-than-expected core inflation and a fresh round of U.S. tariff proposals. Bitcoin had traded near $58,400 before the 8:30 a.m. ET data release. Bitcoin slipped to $60,000 on Tuesday morning and lost that level later in the day. It has now given back all of Monday’s spike above $64,000, which faded within hours after Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO. The bitcoin price remains above the weekend low near $55,100, its lowest level in more than two years. The world’s largest cryptocurrency is down about 24% in November and on course for its worst month since 2022. It has also lost more than 30% since the start of the year, as record ETF outflows, rising rate-hike bets and a slide in AI stocks have kept buyers on the sidelines. Nasdaq sinks 4% as tech selloff spreads The selling spread from Asia, where South Korea’s Kospi fell 6.16% overnight, to Wall Street. The Nasdaq Composite tumbled about 4% in early trading, while the S&P 500 fell about 3% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost about 2%. Nvidia sank more than 8% to near $142, and Micron and AMD each fell more than 9% as doubts over the returns on AI spending resurfaced. Tariffs added to the risk-off mood. The Trump administration proposed new Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China, the European Union, Japan and India, over what it calls excess industrial capacity. China faces a 20% duty on top of the 25% imposed in 2018, CNBC reported. The new duties would take effect after a public comment period, in January at the earliest. PCE data and Fed hike bets weigh on the bitcoin price Inflation came in hotter than expected. The personal consumption expenditures price index rose 0.3% in October and 3.8% from a year earlier, the Commerce Department said. Core PCE, which excludes food and energy and is the Fed’s preferred gauge, climbed 3.3% from a year ago, above the 3.2% economists had expected and up from 3.1% in September. Growth also ran hot. Real gross domestic product increased at a 4.3% annual rate in the third quarter, the Bureau of Economic Analysis said in its second estimate, up from the 3.4% pace first reported. Reuters called it the fastest growth in three years, driven by consumer spending and business investment in AI. The reports solidified bets on another rate increase, with traders pricing in a 98% chance of a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting. The 10-year Treasury yield fell more than 6 basis points to 4.84% as investors bought bonds for protection, but that offered little support to the bitcoin price. ETF selling continues. item.title: France’s Senate Rejects Rule Forcing Bitcoin Holders to Declare Self-Custody Wallets
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine France’s Senate Rejects Rule Forcing Bitcoin Holders to Declare Self-Custody Wallets France’s Senate has rejected a proposal that would have forced bitcoin holders to report self-custody wallets worth €100,000 or more to the tax authorities, along with two other crypto tax measures in the 2027 budget. Senators voted down two identical amendments on Nov. 24 during debate on the first part of the 2027 finance bill. Both would have required taxpayers to declare crypto wallets they hold directly, outside a crypto service provider, when the total value inside reached at least €100,000 on Dec. 31 of the tax year. The first, amendment I-2447 , came from Sens. Pascal Savoldelli and Pierre Barros and the Communist-led CRCE-K group. The second, amendment I-2992 , came from Sen. Anne-Sophie Romagny and seven other senators. The government opposed both, and both were rejected. The case for a wallet rule in France Backers argued that France already makes taxpayers declare accounts on foreign crypto platforms, just like foreign bank accounts. Wallets that holders manage themselves, without an intermediary, escape any such obligation. “They have become the digital equivalent of the undeclared safe,” the CRCE-K group wrote in its amendment, adding that tax authorities can’t see them, check gains on them or reach them in an estate or when a holder moves abroad. Romagny’s version pointed to a gap in the numbers. Crypto holders in France realized €3.5 billion in gains in 2021, but only €400 million in digital assets were declared to the tax administration that same year, the amendment said. It proposed fines of up to €10,000 for failing to declare. The National Assembly had approved the same wallet rule on Nov. 3. It fell away the next day, when deputies rejected the entire revenue section of the budget. Senators then took up the same measure as an amendment to the budget. Stablecoin swaps and exit tax also rejected Senators also rejected two other proposals from the CRCE-K group. Amendment I-2421 would have ended France’s tax deferral on swaps into electronic money tokens under the EU’s MiCA rules. That would have made converting bitcoin into a regulated stablecoin a taxable event. Amendment I-2428 would have pulled crypto into France’s exit tax on unrealized gains for people who move their tax home abroad. It counted all crypto toward the €800,000 threshold, including coins held in self-custody or outside France. David Amiel, France’s minister for public action and accounts, argued against the wallet rule, saying the EU’s DAC8 directive already puts reporting duties on crypto firms. He said he was “more circumspect” about a “purely declarative” obligation that would not help authorities track crypto used in money laundering or tax fraud. The Senate’s finance committee also opposed the measures, and rapporteur general Christine Lavarde recommended rejecting all three. item.title: Microsoft fixes Office dialog that had nothing to say and wouldn't go away
item.description: Microsoft has released a fix for a baffling bug that threw a blank window over Office applications and brought work to a standstill. The problem appeared when users launched an affected Office app, which could display an empty dialog box with no text and no buttons. Because the dialog offered no way to close it, some users were locked out of their work entirely, unable to continue until the issue was resolved. The good news is that there's an update to fix the problem – version 2611, build 16.0.20625.20142. The bad news is that you might not be able to launch the applications to perform the update because of that blank dialog window. Microsoft instructs affected users to save their work, close all Office applications, and open Command Prompt as administrator. They can then force the update with: "%programfiles%\Common Files\Microsoft Shared\ClickToRun\officec2rclient.exe" /update user updatetoversion=16.0.20625.20142 The glitch affects a swathe of Microsoft 365 products – Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Access, and OneNote. Users reported the problem on Microsoft's forums , where volunteer moderator Stefan Blom noted that "this seems to be a common error at the moment" and suggested users try an Office repair or the more thorough Online Repair. Online Repair reinstalls Office, however, some users reported activation and sign-in problems alongside the blank windows, which may hint at the cause. Microsoft has yet to elucidate. Other users found that rolling back Office resolved the issue, while several reported that signing in with another application, such as Edge, fixed things. For administrators preparing fleets of devices, a dialog that blocks first use creates another deployment headache. One user with E3 licensing reported: "We can't just hand off a staged machine without getting call[s] that our new users can't get Office to work because of the blank licensing window." Microsoft has shared a fix for the problem, but has not stated which versions of its productivity applications were affected, nor has it explained what went wrong. The fix is welcome. An explanation of how Office ended up blocking users with a window containing nothing at all would be welcome too. ®

item.description: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said it has dismantled another industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory in Enugu State. It also said that it arrested a 63-year-old drug baron it identified as one “Chuks Enoch Ezeike, popularly known as ‘Over Size’,” and five Mexican meth specialists whom he allegedly smuggled into the country with forged passports to produce the Class A drug on Nigerian soil. ﻿ The NDLEA disclosed that a total of 1,512 kilograms of methamphetamine, finished and in production, with an estimated value of US$226.8 million, equivalent to ₦303,913,000,000.00, was recovered from the clandestine factory, alongside 6.68 tons of 20 different types of precursor and essential chemicals and an array of industrial equipment for making the illicit substance. “Ezeike, a businessman who holds the traditional title of Ebekuo Dike na Nanka in his community in Anambra State, had built the industrial complex behind San Savanna Oil Company Limited, at Kilometre 1/2 Abakaliki Expressway, Emene, Enugu, complete with living quarters for the Mexicans so they could live and produce in the same place without being seen in town,” Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of the agency, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Marwa (retd.) said at a press conference in Abuja on Wednesday. Marwa described it as one of the most carefully planned, intelligence-led operations ever conducted by the agency, adding that the operation “began in faraway Mexico, ran through Colombia, France and the Republic of Benin, crossed into Lagos, and ended in an industrial complex in Enugu.” He explained that the agency’s Special Operations Unit (SOU) began working on critical intelligence in April 2026, which identified Ezeike as a specialist in setting up clandestine methamphetamine laboratories with links to one Oscar Ramos-Cardenas, alleged to be a Mexican known for large-scale, industrial-grade methamphetamine production. “From that moment, Ezeike was a marked man. Our officers opened a file on him, and we watched and waited,” the NDLEA chief was quoted as saying in a statement by the agency’s Director, Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi. “On 25th August 2026, we received intelligence on the flight itineraries of five Mexican nationals, all identified as methamphetamine experts who were travelling from Mexico to Nigeria. Our analysis left no room for doubt: they were coming to set up an industrial-scale meth laboratory on Nigerian soil. “Working closely with the Nigeria Immigration Service, we ensured that when they landed here in Abuja on 28th August 2026, they were denied entry. They were put on the next available flight back to Mexico. “On that same day, our officers found out that Ezeike had travelled from Enugu to Abuja to receive the visiting Mexicans. His own bank records later confirmed the hotel payment in Abuja that day. The visitors he came to receive were the very men we had just sent back”, Marwa stated. item.title: A familiar Iranian hacking group has found a new way to cause chaos
item.description: One night in October, hackers staged one of the most unusual cyber attacks in history : cranking up the temperature in refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets across France and destroying millions of euros of food. Hackers have targeted commercial fridges and freezers before, but never at this scale and never in the heart of Europe. The brazen attack left cyber professionals unsure as to who might have executed such a madcap operation. But French intelligence agencies found traces of Farsi and other clues in the digital trail pointing to an elite hacking unit of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The unit allegedly behind the hack, Shahid Kaveh, was already well known to Western intelligence agencies. Named after Mahmoud Kaveh, an Iranian commander who died during the 1980s Iran-Iraq war, it is one of several hacking units overseen by the Revolutionary Guards’ Cyber Electronic Command. item.title: JetBrains finds agents may cheat with open source
item.description: JetBrains has revamped a benchmark for evaluating large language models after suspecting too many agents gamed their tasks the first time round. The company labelled this agentic practice "reward hacking" in a post summarizing the results of its revised evaluation. Like its predecessor , Kotlin Benchmark 2.0 is a collection of tasks that evaluates how well AI coding agents work with the Kotlin programming language , in order to help Kotlin programmers decide which agent-model configurations to use. The tasks include fixing tricky problems in Kotlin code across different domains, and making corrections to multiple files. Dirty data The revised benchmar k now includes 30 Kotlin multi-file code problems that have not been exposed to the public in any way before. The revised test all but guarantees that the agents have not encountered this set of problems, or potential solutions, before. Another 70 tasks are based on code that resides in public repositories. The test also blocked all network access for the open source tasks, except for what was needed to communicate with the model itself. This minimized the possibility that the agent could look for an existing answer already posted, perhaps through a patch or pull request. A 30-minute limit was set for each task. Overall, the agents were significantly less accurate when solving problems on codebases they had never encountered. Top resolution rates dropped rather suspiciously from 86.2 percent on tasks based on open source repositories to 60 percent on those based on closed source repositories. Although the agents lacked network access, JetBrains boffins theorized that they might have benefited from encountering and internalizing these open source repositories during training. Only the private repositories were completely new to them. Also curious was how a different set of models excelled at the closed source problems, compared to those models that usually did better on the open source tasks. Leaderboard Shakeup When restricted to closed source tasks, two dark horse models rose to the top: Gemini 3.8 Flash, via Antigravity CLI, topped the list with a 60 percent success rate, closely followed by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (running on OpenCode) at 58.9 percent. Of the two, the open weight DeepSeek was far cheaper (at $0.08 per task) than the closed weight Gemini ($1.74 per task), however. In contrast, Opus 5.5 completed only 53.3 percent of the tasks at $1.21 per task, and Fable 5.1 completed only 44.4 percent of the tasks, at a luxurious $3.27 per task. Claude Code harnessed both of these models. Claude’s lackluster completion rates on closed source tasks are somewhat sus given how both of these Anthropic models scored significantly higher on tasks using open source materials. In fact Claude ran the table when it came to open source: Fable 5.1 topped the charts with 86.2 percent accuracy, closely followed by Opus 5.5 at 84.8 percent accuracy. item.title: Xteink’s pocketable X4 Classic e-reader is down to just $55 for Black Friday
item.description: Unsurprisingly, we’re already seeing some solid Black Friday deals on a wide variety of e-readers. Everything from the Kobo Libra Colour to last-gen Kindle Paperwhite is on sale, but if you’re looking for something much cheaper — or considerably smaller — the Xteink X4 Classic is in a league of its own. Thankfully, the tiny e-reader is down to a new low of $54.87 ($55 off) at Amazon , making it an especially affordable alternative to Amazon’s latest Kindle. Xteink X4 Classic pocket e-reader Where to Buy: $109 $54.87 at Amazon (black) $109 $54.87 at Amazon (white) $109 $59 at Xteink The X4 Classic is an updated version of Xteink’s original pocket-sized e-reader, one that features a miniature 4.3-inch E Ink display that makes it more pocketable than any current Kindle or Kobo model. Like the pricier X4 Pro — which also happens to be on sale direct from Xteink for $84 — it features both physical page-turning buttons and magnets that let you attach it to compatible smartphones. At just 2.4 ounces and 4.9mm thick, it’s also easy to slip into a pocket, while its larger 920mAh battery can last up to 10 days on a single charge. That said, unlike the X4 Pro , the Classic lacks a touchscreen and built-in reading light, meaning you’ll need an external light to read in the dark. It also uses a proprietary magnetic charging connector instead of USB-C, and transferring books isn’t as straightforward as on a Kindle or Kobo. However, like the Pro, it does support the excellent CrossPoint Reader software , which you can install yourself to improve the reading experience. You can even use it to read books borrowed through Libby or purchased from stores like Kobo, though it takes a few extra steps to do so. Still, if you want an inexpensive, distraction-free way to read on the go, the X4 Classic is hard to beat for less than half the price of a Kindle. Read our hands-on impressions of the Xteink X4.

item.title: Watch live: Europe unveils 1st close-up views of asteroid Dimorphos after NASA's DART impact
item.description: null After a two-year journey, the Hera spacecraft is arriving at the Didymos double asteroid system, and its first images are being released to the public today (Nov. 25). The European Space Agency's (ESA's ) Hera probe launched atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Oct. 7, 2024 . Its destination is the Didymos-Dimorphos asteroid system, which consists of the larger Didymos , a " rubble pile" asteroid , and its smaller moonlet Dimorphos. NASA slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in 2022 in the historic DART test , which confirmed that such an impact can alter the trajectory of an asteroid. Hera arrives at Didymos today, and ESA is sharing the first close-up images from the mission in a free online livestream. ESA's livestream starts at 1:45 p.m. ET (1845 GMT) on Wednesday (Nov. 25) . Watch it live here, courtesy of the European Space Agency. At Dimorphos, Hera will inspect the wreckage caused by DART (Double Asteroid Redirect Test), humanity's first test of planetary defense. The test was designed to see if the orbit of a threatening asteroid could be altered, taking it off a potential crash course with Earth. A simulation of the impact of DART on Didymos (Image credit: S.D. Raducan) The DART mission succeeded, shortening Dimorphos' orbit by just over 30 minutes, showing that kinetic impacts can indeed alter the trajectories of asteroids. Hera will now show up to the crash scene and study the impact crater left by DART and inspect any changes the collision caused. Scientists are thrilled by the prospects. A series of images captured by the DART spacecraft as it sped to impact the asteroid Dimorphos on Sept. 26, 2022. (Image credit: NASA/JHUAPL) "ESA's Hera mission has arrived to learn the answers we need to know," the mission's principal investigator Patrick Michel said in an ESA statement . "How did the impact change Dimorphos? What is the mass of the asteroid and which of its properties explain its response to DART impact? "Hera is carrying out a thorough investigation ever of a deflected asteroid, packed with scientific firsts, to give us a complete and unbiased picture of humankind's first planetary defense test." A view of Didymos from ESA's Hera spacecraft. (Image credit: ESA) ESA has already shared some of the remarkable images Hera has captured en route to Didymos, including a breathtaking image of both asteroids as Dimorphos cast its shadow on its larger companion in a deep-space double-asteroid solar eclipse . Hera even stopped by Mars on its way to the asteroids, snapping pictures of its moon Deimos . The image shows the Didymos double asteroid system, which consists of the larger Didymos and its moonlet, Dimorphos. In this image, Dimorphos' shadow can be seen on the surface of Didymos. (Image credit: ESA) Hera will remain at the Didymos-Dimorphos system for months, deploying cubesats that will study the asteroids with visible and infrared light cameras and radar instruments. item.title: Debian wakes up wearing Windows XP's actual skin
item.description: Win4Wine is one of the more remarkable and creative hacks we've read about in recent years. It runs Windows XP's genuine Explorer shell through patched Wine on Debian 13, with a custom window manager integrating Linux applications into the desktop. As its GitHub repository explains: "The taskbar, Start menu, desktop and folder windows are XP's real ones, and Linux applications get XP's frames and taskbar buttons." This impressive, possibly demented project has English installation instructions and a README, although its design documents are in Japanese. We found Mozilla's built-in translation handled those pretty well. Its developer goes by miKuta0407 on GitHub, their homepage , and X . Also note, you're going to need some Windows installation media for the full experience. The README says: "No Microsoft files are included. Only the files that are needed are extracted locally from your own ISO." It supports Windows XP Professional SP3 installation images in 32-bit Japanese or English editions, with an experimental option for Windows 7 SP1 x64. Without either Windows image, it can download and use ReactOS's free software shell instead, for what it terms "a Windows 2000-like classic look." In our view, that sounds much better anyway. Before any former Windows users cry hurray and reach for an optical drive, this is not some ready-to-run project. The top of the README warns: "This is a personal, experimental project, not a finished product for daily use." The developer has tested it only on a fresh Debian 13 installation and recommends a VM or spare machine, rather than an existing working desktop, which sounds like an excellent precaution to us. Also, before you ask, yes, it was vibe-coded with Claude. We found ourselves reminded of another crazy-but-is-it project that we wrote about back in January: What if Linux ran Windows... and meant it? Meet Loss32 . The Loss32 proposal was even more extreme. It suggested replacing essentially the entire Linux userland, so it would be a Linux kernel running Wine with a Windows desktop and Windows apps. However, Mikuta-san was way ahead of us – lower down, the README mentions and even links to Loss32. Saying that, since it launched at the end of 2025, the bottom of the Loss32 web page shows a couple of updates, reporting on delays in getting it working. That, to be honest, did not shock us, but we still admire the let's-do-this spirit. The developer also seems to have got slightly distracted by a previous project, touchHLE: high-level emulator for early iOS apps . Loss32, in turn, reminded us of Neptune OS, an attempt to give seL4 a Windows personality transplant . We wrote about that back in 2022, and work on it has continued: the project page shows updates in recent months. The team has also pushed out preview releases in 2022, 2024, 2025, and most recently in September. This OS face transplant also reminded us of our article, Classic 7 is Windows 10 LTSC cosplaying as Windows 7 . Some people really miss the
