item.title: Nollywood Stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Others Pay Tribute To Pete Edochie
item.description: Nollywood stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Mercy Johnson and others have paid tributes to veteran actor Pete Edochie, who died Wednesday after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer at the age of 79. The actor’s death was announced by his son, Chief Leo Pete Edochie, who confirmed that he died at 12:30 a.m. on November 25, 2026, in Enugu, Nigeria. His death has sparked an outpouring of tributes from colleagues, public leaders and entertainers who have celebrated his remarkable career, influence and legacy. Actress Joke Silva expressed sadness over his death, remembering his playful side. “Uncle Pete…I will miss your teasing. Rest well Sir,” she wrote. Filmmaker and actress Funke Akindele recalled growing up watching Edochie in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart , before eventually sharing the screen with him in the film Egg of Life . She expressed gratitude for his encouragement and the impact he made on younger generations of actors. “Thank you for paving the way for so many of us in Nollywood and for being an inspiration to us over the years. Your work lives on,” she wrote. Similarly, actress Uche Jombo described Edochie as one of Nollywood’s greatest pillars, a master of his craft and a custodian of Nigerian culture. She said the late actor “gave Nigerian storytelling a face, a voice and a legacy that will outlive generations.” “His contribution to Nollywood cannot be measured by the number of films he appeared in, but by the impact he made, the standards he set and the generations of actors he inspired.” Actress Omoni Oboli described his passing as the fall of an iroko tree, writing, “Hmmm 2026! It is well. The Iroko has fallen. Rest in power sir Pete Edochie.” May Edochie, the estranged wife of the late actor’s son, Yul Edochie, also paid tribute, describing him as an institution and a father figure to many. She reflected on the false reports of his death that had circulated over the years, noting that he had continued working despite the rumours. Actor Charles Inojie paid tribute using several of the late actor’s traditional praise names, including Ebube Dike, Ntu Mara Igwe and King of the Forests, before praying for his peaceful rest. While DJ Kaywise thanked him for his contributions to the industry, other entertainers who expressed their grief included comedian Sabinus, who described Edochie as an oracle and a legend. Pete Edochie was born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State. His ancestral roots, however, trace back to Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State. Edochie rose to prominence through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the 1987 Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart . item.title: Ebola Fight Runs Up Against Customs, Rites In Remote DR Congo
item.description: For health workers in the volatile eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), tackling local suspicions is as big a problem as combating the Ebola virus that has plagued it for six months. In the rural community of Bulambo-Isale, AFP saw a small crowd gather this week along a dirt track, determined to prevent an ambulance bringing the body of a local Ebola victim for burial. Victims of the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever, which spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids, must be interred in sealed body bags to prevent infection spreading from the corpse. Burial ceremonies are conducted by specially trained health workers, anonymous in protective hazmat suits, some of whom locals allege are brought in from outside the community and do not speak the local languages. In this file photo taken on March 09, 2019 Health workers are seen inside the ‘red zone’ of an Ebola treatment centre, which was attacked in the early hours of the morning in Butembo. – Democratic Republic of Congo’s government on June 25, 2020 officially declared an end to an epidemic of Ebola that broke out in the east of the troubled country in August 2018 and went on to claim 2,277 lives. (Photo by JOHN WESSELS / AFP) But custom dictates that the deceased be buried by their own family and their body be allowed to fuse with the earth of their ancestors. “The authorities have imposed the Ebola response on locals without first making sure how they interpret it,” grumbled Patricien Kambale, who became a livestock farmer after university. “The sick victim gets carted away in a vehicle and locals don’t know where they’re being taken. Then we learn later that the person has died so locals think the doctors are using poisoned medicine to kill people,” he said. Suspicions of ‘profiteering’ Health workers in Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) simulate with the help of an Outbreak Response Advisor admission protocols of suspected cases during a training by medical charity, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) to reinforce regional emergency response capacity for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo Locals say they are distrustful of Congolese authorities, who have a reputation for corruption and nepotism. Left to cope with the miseries inflicted by myriad armed groups that have stalked their mineral-rich region for more than three decades, they fear their customs and lives matter little to the powers that be. Wilson Kasyani, chief doctor for the Vuhovi health district that includes Bulambo-Isale, a rural settlement in North Kivu province, was worried for the ambulance and its occupants. “Weapons are everywhere” in the mountainous region, he said. Medical workers face almost daily attacks due to locals’ hostility to efforts to respond to the Ebola outbreak, which has killed more than 5,000 people out of more than 11,000 cases since May. “Today, people entered a nurse’s home and wounded her son,” Kasyani said wearily. “And yesterday we had to stop someone who wanted to attack invest

item.title: Astronomers discover the most distant and ancient supermassive black hole-powered quasar in the universe
item.description: null The Euclid space telescope has spotted the most distant and ancient quasar ever seen, a bright cosmic event powered by a supermassive black hole with 360 million times the mass of the sun. The supermassive black hole is seen as it was just 630 million years after the Big Bang. 40 million years further back in time than the previous record holder for the most ancient quasar. The discovery further deepens the mystery of how supermassive black holes grew so massive so soon into the history of the universe. That's because previously, scientists had theorized it should take 1 billion years of feeding and merging for black holes to reach supermassive status of millions or billions of times as massive as the sun. Quasars occur when supermassive black holes are surrounded by vast amounts of gas and dust on which they feed. The immense gravitational influence of the black hole causes this material, in the form of an accretion disk, to glow brightly and to blast out bright jets of plasma. That means quasars at the heart of galaxies in regions called active galactic nuclei (AGNs) like this one can often be brighter than the combined light of every star in the entire surrounding galaxy, but only briefly. The newly discovered quasar, designated J1504+6252 and nicknamed Dún Aonghasa, is in this brief phase of its existence. It was discovered among millions of objects in 18 months of data from Euclid. Euclid's initial observation of Dún Aonghasa was followed up by an array of ground-based and space-based telescopes, including the W.M. Keck Observatory, the Large Binocular Telescope Observatory, the Hubble Space Telescope , and ultimately the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). It was the JWST that determined the mass of this supermassive black hole. What is interesting about Dún Aonghasa is that it is unlike other supermassive black holes seen at a similar period of the early universe. That's because this black hole is feeding relatively slowly. That means if it engaged in rapid feeding to reach its massive size, that period of gorging on gas and dust has either ended or it has paused. The red dot at the center of this Euclid image is Dún Aonghasa (Image credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, Wolf et al. 2026) That is something that further complicates our picture of supermassive black hole growth. By staring back 13.1 billion years in time to see Dún Aonghasa, Euclid is also observing a crucial time in cosmic history when the first stars and galaxies were taking shape, and the clearing of cosmic gas was ending the dark ages of our universe by allowing light to travel freely. Euclid's primary mission is improving our understanding of dark energy , the mysterious force accelerating the expansion of the universe, and dark matter , the most mysterious "stuff" in the cosmos. Collectively, these aspects of the universe account for around 95% of its matter-energy budget and have come to be collectively referred to as the dark universe. Hence Euclid's nickname

item.title: Microsoft 365 Backup stretches recovery window to ten years
item.description: Recovery windows of up to ten years are now available in Microsoft 365 Backup for OneDrive and SharePoint, up from a previous maximum of two. The change took effect on October 31, though Exchange remains capped at two years. Administrators can select recovery windows of three months, six months, or any whole number of years from one to ten. Microsoft's list price is $0.15 per GiB per month of protected content. Extended windows can increase costs by keeping deleted data billable for longer. Switching to a longer recovery window will also not make backups for that period magically available. So no nostalgic trips back to 2016. Wider recovery windows may appeal to organizations that need access to older data, but backups are not a substitute for compliance retention and archiving. Recovery after a breach or ransomware attack is also critical, particularly getting back to a healthy state before any malware seeped into files. Microsoft says backups are physically redundant and geographically replicated while respecting the tenant's data residency requirements. Full OneDrive account and SharePoint site restores offer recovery points every ten minutes for the most recent two weeks, then weekly points through the configured window, up to ten years. Individual file and folder recovery is limited to recovery points from the most recent 14 days, regardless of the configured window. Restore remains free, which is handy since regular testing is a vital part of any disaster recovery plan. The arrival of a ten-year recovery window is good for enterprises that need it and have deep enough pockets. However, it is important to keep in mind that being able to configure a longer recovery window doesn't constitute a disaster recovery plan in itself and may be overkill in many instances. Microsoft notes: "The existing one-year default recovery window remains unchanged. Longer recovery windows must be configured on the applicable backup policies." The company also recommends that users "review your organization's SharePoint and OneDrive backup requirements to determine whether longer recovery windows are needed." A decade of recovery history could be valuable. It also means a decade of data to account for when setting budgets, access controls, and retention policies. ®

item.title: Amazon to flog motors in Britain, but Prime won't deliver
item.description: Amazon is channeling its inner car salesman as it prepares to flog motors on the UK arm of its online tat bazaar. Amazon Autos will launch in Britain in early 2027, its first expansion outside the US, where it debuted in December 2024. Customers can browse and reserve cars online before completing the purchase with a dealer. Hoping it will be "a nice little earner," Amazon will let punters view real-time dealer inventory, prices, get an instant trade-in valuation, and connect with a local dealer to reserve a car, "all on Amazon." In the US, the service now covers more than 150 cities and offers vehicles from 35 brands. Hyundai is the first announced UK carmaker partner, while dealer group Vertu Motors will list used vehicles. More brands and dealers are due to be confirmed before launch. Hyundai's launch range will include electric, hybrid, and petrol models. "Buying a car is one of the biggest purchases people make, and we think it should feel as simple and transparent as shopping for anything on Amazon," said Matt Nuffort, director of Amazon Autos International. Of course, buying a car isn't quite like adding an air fryer or a memory stick to your basket. How does financing and checkout work for UK buyers? Customers will complete the purchase and paperwork at their chosen dealership. Amazon is not offering financing itself, but buyers can explore financing options via the site, adjusting terms like deposit and duration to see how monthly payments change. Credit applications must be completed with the dealer. In the US, buyers can submit a credit application through the platform, review terms and conditions, then sign electronic contracts online. They typically pay a deposit and visit the dealership to complete the remaining paperwork and pick up the vehicle. Buyers shouldn't expect their new car to arrive in an enormous cardboard box with a smiley logo on it, or to be lowered onto their driveway by a giant Amazon delivery drone. But given that one of the online retailer's flying delivery robots crashed into someone's garage after making a drop-off near Detroit last week, perhaps that's for the best. ®

item.title: AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist
item.description: About six months ago, Suvrat Raju, a professor of theoretical physics at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences in Bengaluru, India, asked a frontier AI model to solve a physics problem. He didn’t ask because he needed to know the answer. He had actually solved this particular problem already. But he had never published the solution—which made it a perfect question to test how good AI was at physics. LLMs have been trained on the whole Internet, so if a physics problem has been discussed online, it’s likely the model already knows about it and may have memorized the answer. So a fair test of AI capabilities needs to focus on problems that have never appeared online. The model didn’t answer Raju’s problem correctly, but it did better than he expected—well, enough to get him thinking that the experiment should be repeated and formalized. With the help of a colleague, he set out to create a theoretical physics benchmark for AI. Read full article Comments

item.title: November's full moon dazzles skywatchers with a stunning Beaver Moon supermoon (photos)
item.description: null The November full moon rose to put on a spectacular natural light show on Nov. 24 and we've got the photos to prove it! Read on to see our favorite shots of the "Beaver Moon" captured from around the world. Each monthly full moon has its own set of informal names , often bestowed to reflect events occurring in the world at the time of their rising. The November moon is often known as the Beaver Moon, a name associated with the time of year when beavers prepare for winter and when trappers historically set beaver traps before waterways froze. November's full moon served as the opening salvo in a series of four dazzling supermoons , which turn full around the time that the natural satellite passes closest to Earth in its 27-day elliptical orbit. That added proximity can make it appear noticeably brighter and larger than the smallest full moon of the year, setting the stage for an incredible photo shoot as the lunar disk climbed high into the autumn sky. Best photos of the November 2026 full Beaver Moon Our first shot of the moon was captured by photographer Pongmanat Tasiri as the moon rose over the roof of the Wat Phra That Doi Suthep Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai Province, Thailand, as a stunning array of craters and lunar seas scar the Beaver Moon's surface. The Beaver Moon takes flight into the night sky. (Image credit: Photo by Pongmanat Tasiri/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images) Meanwhile, Gary Hershorn snapped a gorgeous shot of the full yellow moon rising over the Chrysler Building in New York, with the Empire State Building and myriad other skyscrapers dominating the skyline. The Beaver Moon rises over the New York skyline. (Image credit: Photo by Gary Hershorn/Getty Images) Hershorn also managed to line up a colorful shot of the lunar disk glowing between the concrete canyon of New York's iconic 42nd Street just before moonset on the morning of Nov. 24, mere hours before the moon turned full. The moon shines between a concrete canyon in New York. (Image credit: Photo by Gary Hershorn/Getty Images) Our next photo was captured by Space.com's Skywatching Editor Daisy Dobrijevic using a Sony A7IV with a Tamron 50-400mm lens as the moon shone in the skies over the city of Nottingham in the U.K. on Nov. 23. "Having seen the rather disappointing weather forecast for the night of the full moon, I decided to head out a day early and capture the almost-full Beaver Moon instead," explained Dobrijevic. "It hadn’t quite risen above the rooftops of the houses opposite me, so I took a peek down the alleyway and, sure enough, there it was, nestled between two houses, giving me just enough of a clear view to capture this close-up." Bright ejecta rays stretch across ancient lunar lava plains in this close-up of the nearly full Beaver Moon captured from Nottingham, U.K. (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic) This striking image of the full moon rising above the Toronto skyline was snapped by Mert Alper Dervis as a flock of birds skimmed through the for

item.title: The world's fastest computers have a problem: Keeping the work running
item.description: Frontier, Oak Ridge National Laboratory's exascale supercomputer, has thousands of processors working together on scientific problems. It also has a surprisingly ordinary way of ruining a researcher's day: one node going down. An uncorrectable memory error can do it, or a maintenance mishap. Scott Atchley , chief technology officer at the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility, describes technicians accidentally rebooting the wrong node or risking a neighboring node's power supply while working in tightly packed racks. The hardware fault can affect just one node, but a simulation running across thousands of processors can grind to a halt. Then comes a series of questions. How recently did the application save its progress? How much computation needs repeating? And how long before the scheduler lets the job run again? For operators, the challenge isn't just keeping the supercomputer running. It's keeping the science moving. One bad node and everybody suffers On Frontier , a memory error can have an outsized audience. Atchley says uncorrectable double-bit errors in high-bandwidth memory occurred about 1.5 times a day during the supercomputer's early bring-up. Its predecessor, Summit, saw roughly one every two weeks. This sounds like a backward step, until you count the memory. Frontier has more than 16 times as much, giving bad bits considerably more places to hide. Memory isn't the only problem. Problematic GPU firmware can crash a node, and so can a technician rebooting the wrong one. Interconnect faults add another way for a large job to come unstuck. In a tightly coupled simulation using the Message Passing Interface (MPI) simulation, thousands of processes, or ranks, exchange data and participate in collective operations. If one rank disappears, the others cannot carry on as though nothing happened. Clockwork.io CEO Suresh Vasudevan describes a similar dependency in synchronized GPU training. One failed GPU can bring a 1,024-GPU job to a pause. An underperforming GPU can be almost as troublesome: if one participant runs at 80 percent speed, others might have to spend time waiting for it. The bigger the machine, the more ways there are for one small problem to become everybody's problem. How often should you hit save? Since stopping every component from failing isn't an option, researchers need a way to preserve their work. That's where checkpointing comes in. The application periodically saves its state so that, when something goes wrong, the simulation can resume from an earlier point instead of starting from scratch. The catch is that saving progress costs computing time, and doing it too often can become almost as wasteful as losing the work itself. Vasudevan explains this with an example. If writing a checkpoint takes 30 seconds, saving every five minutes consumes roughly 10 percent of computing time. Stretch that interval to 50 minutes, and the overhead drops to about 1 percent. item.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
item.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). Veteran Nollywood actor Chief Dr Pete Edochie and his wife, Barrister Mrs Josephine Edochie, at a church service. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Chief Dr Pete Edochie is survived by his beloved wife of over five decades, Barrister Mrs Josephine Edochie, their six children—Leo, Adam, Linc, Jean, Yul, and Eva Edochie (with Linc and Yul following closely in his acting footsteps)—as well as his siblings, grandchildren, and extended family. item.title: Jury finds Huawei stole US tech, laundered money, and broke sanctions
item.description: A US jury has found Chinese tech giant Huawei stole tech from American companies, laundered money, and violated sanctions by building major internet infrastructure for Iran, but didn’t operate an illegal racket to get that done. This case kicked off in 2020, when the US Department of Justice claimed entities Huawei operated in America violated federal law. The indictment led to a trial on a dozen criminal matters that has played out over the last three months in the Eastern District Court of New York. The trial ended on Tuesday when a jury found Huawei and three subsidiary companies guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, conspiracy to commit wire and bank fraud, wire fraud, bank fraud, conspiracy to defraud the United States, conspiracy to violate the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) and substantive violations of that law, plus money laundering conspiracy. The Department of Justice’s celebration of the decision says Huawei was found to have stolen Cisco’s source code, after prosecutors showed evidence that “Huawei engineers left Cisco’s notes about the Cisco code, referred to Cisco using its name backwards ‘ocsic’ and described that portions of the code remained as they existed in the ‘ocsic’ code.” Another item of evidence apparently showed a Huawei staffer photographing Fujitsu equipment while wearing a fake employee badge for a company called “Weihua” – cunningly reversing the two syllables of “Huawei.” Another allegation the jury accepted involved Huawei staffers signing a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) ahead of a visit to T-Mobile to inspect a robot the telco created to test mobile devices. Huawei staff ignored that NDA so thoroughly that they “sent photographs and technical details of the robot back to China” so the Chinese company could make its own robot. “When that data was not sufficient, a Huawei employee stole a part of the robot in his backpack and carried it out of T-Mobile’s controlled laboratory,” the DoJ says. The feds say the Chinese company also “lied about its activities in Iran to banks to obtain billions of U.S. dollars and access to U.S.-dollar clearing services, which enabled Huawei to be a sophisticated participant in a global marketplace for telecommunications services — in part because of its lies.” Huawei has issued a statement noting that the jury found it not guilty of racketeering and insisting the charges on which it was found guilty are “without legal or factual merit.” “The five trade secret-related disputes cited by the government were all civil matters that were resolved over the past two decades,” the statement adds. Sentencing will take place in September 2027. The presiding judge will likely consider the fact that in 2017, US authorities fined Chinese telco equipment maker ZTE $900 million just for selling to Iran, then added an additional $1.4 billion penalty to lift a ban on doing business in the USA. item.title: This could mess with Thanksgiving, says VMware as it drops third critical patch bundle in a week
item.description: VMware has issued its third critical security advisory in a week, this time to warn of four critical flaws and address a total of 23 issues. VMSA-2026-0011 landed on November 24, just five days after two other advisories. VMware’s FAQ for the new advisory includes the following remarks: Because of coordinated disclosure and release pipeline timing this VMSA comes on the heels of VMSA-2026-0009, and atop a major holiday in the United States. The security vulnerability landscape is more dynamic than ever; please know that while we acknowledge this timing is not optimal, your ability to operate and maintain a secure environment amidst modern, AI-assisted threats is paramount to us. Make of that what you will as you ponder how and when to patch the four critical flaws, including the 9.8-rated CVE-2026-123903, which allows a malicious actor to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to vCenter, the management tool VMware users rely on to manage hosts and VMs. This is the third 9.8-rated authentication issue VMware has fixed in vCenter since July. Two of the other critical flaws in this new advisory allow an attacker to run code on an ESX host, earning the bugs a 9.8 rating. CVE-2026-123910 makes that possible thanks to a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the I/O filter service, while CVE-2026-123911 is a use-after-free vulnerability. The other critical flaw, CVE-2026-123912, can result in a guest escape from VMware’s desktop Workstation and Fusion desktop hypervisors. It’s also present in VMware’s ESX hypervisor, but attackers thankfully can’t escape that product’s sandbox. This one’s easy to mitigate because the problem is in a USB controller that users can turn off. Most of the other flaws require installation of updated software. There’s a little good news in that some of the software updates VMware issued last week include fixes for the newly disclosed flaws. But there are still plenty of fresh fixes to apply, across ten products: ESX, vCenter, Workstation, Fusion, VMware tools, Cloud Foundation, vSphere Foundation, the Telco Cloud Platform, Telco Cloud Infrastructure, and the VMware Avi Load Balancer. VMware’s advisory thanks external researchers for finding and reporting most of the flaws. The Broadcom business unit is known to be a member of Project Glasswing, the Anthropic-run effort to use the Mythos model to find flaws that has seen many vendors dramatically increase the number of patches they produce. In past years, VMware has often published considerably more than this year’s 11 security advisories. With five weeks left in the year, perhaps vAdmins need to worry Christmas might also get complicated. ®

item.title: Georgia’s Pecan Belt
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Georgia’s Pecan Belt Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search Pecan orchards share the landscape of southwest Georgia with fields of peanuts, cotton, and corn. The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 8 captured this image of the area around Albany on October 23, 2026, during pecan harvest season. NASA Earth Observatory/Lauren Dauphin From the star of its namesake pie to a supporting player in countless side dishes, the pecan has earned a place on Thanksgiving tables across the United States. But before it becomes candied, chopped, or baked, it hangs from the branches of Carya illinoinensis —a species of hickory in the walnut family native to North America. Many U.S.-grown pecans come from orchards in Georgia, the state that has historically led the nation in production. One hotspot of pecan cultivation is in the southwest part of the state, around Albany, in Dougherty County. The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 8 captured this image of the area and neighboring counties on October 23, 2026. That date falls within the pecan harvest season, which typically runs from October into December . In addition to pecans, other crops such as peanuts, cotton, and corn are also grown in the area. Landsat observations like these contribute to the Cropland Data Layer , an annual map of crop types across the contiguous United States produced by the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s National Agricultural Statistics Service . The 2025 map shows pecan groves clustered along the Flint River within the Coastal Plain . Pecan trees need abundant water, and they generally do well in the area’s well-drained sandy soils that sit above the Floridan aquifer system that growers can tap for irrigation. In the late 1800s, Georgia had less than 100 acres (40 hectares) of pecan orchards. Then, in the early 1900s, southwest Georgia’s Dougherty and Mitchell counties underwent a pecan boom when thousands of acres were planted and sold to investors . By the end of the 1950s, Georgia led the nation in pecan production, producing over 17 million pounds, according to 1959 agricultural census numbers . In recent decades, pecan production has grown in other states, such as New Mexico and Texas. Georgia faced challenges after Hurricane Michael damaged orchards in October 2018, and Hurricane Helene dealt another blow when it swept inland in September 2024. Even so, USDA numbers show that the state’s production has topped 100 million pounds in each of the past three years (2023-2025). In 2026, a wet summer in parts of the state helped scab take hold. item.title: Nutanix CEO announces gradual departure, intent to complete set of storage links
item.description: Nutanix CEO Rajiv Ramaswami has decided to step down from the job once the company’s board can find his successor. Ramaswami announced his decision on Tuesday and in conversation with The Register said he doesn’t have another job lined up, isn’t sure what he will do next, fancies sitting on boards or advising startups, but will take a break after Nutanix finds its next leader. The CEO moved from VMware to Nutanix in 2020 and characterized his time at the company as writing its “second chapter.” The first, he explained, saw Nutanix focus on hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI) and a limited group of workloads, especially desktop virtualization, while struggling to make a profit. In chapter two, Nutanix redefined HCI as “hybrid cloud infrastructure” by enabling its stack to run on-prem or in public clouds, and by adding support for containers alongside VMs. Ramaswami took credit for stabilizing Nutanix’s finances while leading the expansion of its platform and for keeping net promoter scores high while the company grew. The CEO added that Nutanix’s decision to end its devotion to virtualized storage and start to support external arrays was also part of chapter two. Ramaswami said he hopes to expand the number of storage vendors Nutanix supports beyond Dell, Everpure, and NetApp, until it works with all major array suppliers. Chapter 3, he said, will be making Nutanix an AI platform, “by catering to a whole new set of ecosystems.” Ramaswami told The Register he had been thinking about moving on for some time and raised it with the board in recent weeks. In the letter he wrote to Nutanix staff , the CEO said the company's board has begun the search for a successor and said he will remain at his post until a replacement is found and then “continue to serve as a senior advisor to the company for a period of time.” News of the CEO’s planned departure came on the same day Nutanix announced its Q1 results, which saw 15 percent revenue growth to $772.4 million. The company added 410 customers in the quarter, the slowest growth for several years. Ramaswami said high hardware costs remain “a headwind” for Nutanix, but said the company continues to win customers seeking an alternative to VMware. He also pointed to the largest new customer win for the quarter coming from a financial services outfit that uses Dell external storage, a significant score because two years ago Nutanix could not have competed for that business. Nutanix forecast slightly faster growth for the rest of its financial year, suggesting it is not ready to ride AI’s rocket to riches. Investors knocked about ten percent off the company’s share price in after-hours trading, sending it to around $50, roughly double what it was when Ramaswami took over as CEO, but below $79-plus peaks in late 2025. ®

item.title: Dell and HPE both say they’ve become ‘different companies’
item.description: Dell and HPE this week both told investors they’ve become “different companies.” The two hardware giants made that assertion on their respective earnings calls this week. HPE went first, on Monday, when CEO Antonio Neri declared “We are now a fundamentally different company” after acquiring Juniper Networks and creating products “built to capitalize on the next phase of AI.” On Tuesday, Dell’s chief operating officer and vice chairman Jeff Clarke declared “We are now a different company” because the Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) has become the source of “the vast majority of our profit and growth.” HPE’s claim to having changed is perhaps more credible on the face of it, given that its acquisition of Juniper means it has become more of a networking player. Dell hasn’t made significant additions to its hardware portfolio, but there’s a big difference in its sources of revenue, which three years ago was just about evenly split between its infrastructure and client devices. In its Tuesday announcement, Dell revealed ISG revenue grew 198 percent year over year to $42 billion, while CSG racked up three percent growth to $12.9 billion – meaning Dell is now predominantly an infrastructure company. Clarke said he’s seen some companies deferring their PC purchases to buy AI hardware instead, and said Dell is re-assigning parts it ordered to build PCs and using them for servers instead. Dell exited its Q3 with a backlog of $32 billion worth of AI servers and is clearly aware that investors might worry that’s not a useful metric because some buyers’ dreams of operating neoclouds have struck financial or regulatory barriers. Clarke assured investors that Dell is “highly selective about the partners we work with” “Every AI order is vetted for access to capital, end customer quality, trade and export compliance, and access to land and power.” HPE also has wrinkles in its AI business, because buyers won’t stand for fat margins and that’s dented the company’s profits a little. Neri was able to point to AI-related revenue also rising sharply, up 68.6 percent year over year to $11.3 billion, while overall revenue climbed 50 percent to reach $14.5 billion. Networking grew at a more relaxed 12 percent. The CEO said HPE expects better growth ahead, because new server purchases create demand for networks and storage. He also pointed to HPE having the opportunity to sell its networking kit to other OEMs who build AMD’s Helios rack-scale systems. HPE predicted its next quarter will see revenue reach $14.0 billion to $14.6 billion, up 51 to 57 percent year over year. Dell is also optimistic that AI buyers will spend on kit beyond servers and GPUs and updated its full-year revenue outlook to $202 billion, $10 billion above its previous forecasts and up 78 percent year over year. ®

item.title: Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical issues
item.description: Two of NASA's four missions operating at Mars have suspended science operations after encountering separate technical issues in recent weeks. The missions affected by the outages — hopefully temporary — are NASA's Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter. Both are operating beyond their original design lifetimes. Perseverance is in its sixth year exploring the surface of Mars, having collected rock and soil samples for eventual return to Earth. The rover is now studying the rim of a crater that once contained an ancient lake of liquid water. Odyssey arrived in orbit around Mars in 2001 and is the longest-lived Mars mission in history. Losing its voice The problem on Perseverance stems from the rover's communications system. The rover has two redundant UHF radios for high-rate communications with a fleet of orbiters that relay data to Earth. A separate X-band system is available for direct-to-Earth communications at a lower data rate. Read full article Comments

item.title: SpaceX launches secretive spy satellites from California for US Space Force (video)
item.description: null SpaceX launched another classified mission for the U.S. Space Force (USSF) today (Nov. 24), sending an unknown payload toward orbit from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Space Launch Complex-4E at TK11:08 a.m. ET (1508 GMT) , carrying the U.S. Space Force's USSF-266 mission. It was the fourth mission SpaceX has launched for the military branch this month. While details about the mission's payload weren't disclosed, it's the fifth space launch in support of U.S. national security in the last two weeks, and comes amid efforts by the Space Force to expand its communications and tracking capabilities. (Image credit: SpaceX) About two and a half minutes after liftoff, Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued toward low Earth orbit with the classified payload. The booster, meanwhile, began a descent toward SpaceX's Of Course I Still Love You droneship in the Pacific Ocean, where it touched down approximately eight and a half minutes after launch. Tuesday's launch marked the 29th flight for this Falcon 9 booster, B1081, which previously launched NASA 's Crew-7 astronaut mission to the International Space Station , the PACE and EarthCARE science satellites , two other classified Space Force launches (USSF-153 and USSF-481), and 16 Starlink missions. Previous classified Space Force launches have fueled speculation about the possible deployment of SpaceX's Starshield satellites, which are designed for national security applications. Starshield is an adapted spacecraft design developed from SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation that supports military operations with capabilities like Earth observation and secure communications. SpaceX has not confirmed whether USSF-266 is carrying Starshield spacecraft. USSF-266 follows three other classified Space Force missions launched by SpaceX from Vandenberg earlier this month: USSF-432 on Nov. 6, USSF-627 on Nov. 11 and USSF-317 on Nov. 20, as well as a National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) launch, NROL-136, on Nov. 22. Those missions were also launched aboard Falcon 9 rockets, also with undisclosed payloads.

item.title: Microsoft's historic cloud outage exposed an engineering “fog of war”
item.description: According to internal memos reviewed by Reuters , Microsoft has declared a "Code Red" overhaul of its engineering response practices after the November 12 outage that lost access to Exchange Online, Teams, and Outlook for users worldwide. Per the memos, Microsoft 365 Core President Jason Henderson described the outage as having the most customer impact in the history of Exchange Online. In a separate memo, Henderson wrote that an urgent production fix in a recent incident took five to six days to reach worldwide saturation. Microsoft's target for its most urgent security fixes is to move from detection to safe worldwide deployment in one hour. "Needless to say, we aren't here yet," Henderson wrote. The memos, which Reuters reviewed but Microsoft has not published, outline the response to the November 12 disruption. The company's post-incident report , dated November 20, attributed the downtime to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July, which caused lock contention in the gateway processes. A Teams traffic failover then dumped additional load onto infrastructure already under stress, as maintenance had left nearly 14 percent of gateway server capacity offline at the time of the incident. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 24, 1947: The US Navy launches the 1st Aerobee sounding rocket, but it didn't reach space
item.description: null On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space. Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere . After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets , the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were launched. Those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space . (NASA and the U.S. military typically consider 50 miles the edge of space.) Mission control cut the flight short after about 30 seconds, because Aerobee started to yaw, and they wanted to keep it from going completely out of control. The first Aerobee sounding rocket launched on Nov. 24, 1947 under a project led by the U.S. Navy. (Image credit: U.S. Navy) Why it mattered Billed as the " most successful sounding rocket of the space age ," the initial Aerobee rocket was suborbital rocket designed to launch experment payload of up to 100 pounds (45 kilograms) to an altitude of 75 miles (121 kilometers) or so. "The Aerobee was designed to carry instruments aloft to collect data on the upper atmosphere and to place small animals in a weightless condition for physiological studies," the U.S. National Museum of the United States Air Force wrote in a mission overview . "It was launched by a solid-propellant booster engine of 18,000 pounds thrust that burned for only two and a half seconds." An Aerobee suborbital sounding rocket of the type designed to study Earth's atmosphere. (Image credit: NMMSH) While the first Aerobee rocket did not reach space , many more made successful launches in the decades that followed. Engineers made a steady stream of upgrades to the the Aerobee rocket, allowing to fly higher and launch heavier payloads into space. It was an Aerobee rocket that launched two Phillipine monkeys on a mission to study how the effects of rapid launch acceleration might affect their bodies, an experiment that was among the frst human physiology tests that paved the way for human spaceflight . More than 1,000 Aerobee rockets have launched since then, and the last one flew in January of 1985. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: NASA+ Content Coming to Big Screen at Greenbelt, Maryland Cinema
item.description: Credit: NASA NASA announced Monday that NASA+ content has found its first theatrical home at The Greenbelt Cinema in Greenbelt, Maryland, expanding the agency’s reach across major viewing platforms and bringing space even closer to home. “The National Aeronautics and Space Act of 1958 calls us to share our story of space exploration with the broadest possible audience, and our partners help us accomplish that,” said Rebecca Sirmons, general manager of NASA+ at the agency’s Headquarters in Washington. “Artemis II captured the imagination of the Artemis generation, but we are just getting started. With Artemis III on the horizon and our sights set on building humanity’s first Moon Base, this is only the beginning of our story being told, and we’ll continue sharing transparent, engaging content every step of the way.” NASA and The Greenbelt Cinema will kick off their partnership with screenings of the NASA+ original documentary “The Europa Concept,” which follows NASA’s journey to investigate the science driving future exploration of Europa, Jupiter’s icy moon. Dates for screenings will be announced soon on NASA.gov. Future programming may include other NASA+ original content, in-person live streaming events of NASA’s Artemis missions, including the first crewed mission to the Moon under the Artemis program, additional Europa content, and more. NASA+ also will remain available for free, with no ads, through the NASA app and on the agency’s website . Earlier this year during its Ignition event, NASA outlined a bold path forward for the agency, including increasing the cadence of Artemis missions to the lunar surface, and building the first Moon Base , among other agency priorities. Partnerships like this one help NASA maximize engagement with communities around the world by making the agency’s missions and educational content available to viewers on their preferred devices and channels. For more information about NASA missions, visit: https://www.nasa.gov Share Details Last Updated Nov 24, 2026 Related Terms NASA+

item.title: Teams Lock in Mission Architecture for NASA’s SR-1 Freedom
item.description: 5 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) NASA’s Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth orbit, cruises past Mars in this artist’s concept, demonstrating nuclear electric propulsion in deep space. Credit: NASA/Jonathan North NASA completed a major review for Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom and locked in key elements of the spacecraft, which is targeted to launch in 2028 and demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion in deep space for the first time. Experts from across the agency, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), and industry met at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland for a major SR-1 mission design review in October. Several key decisions were made, propelling the mission from an early concept toward a defined spacecraft design. “SR-1 marks a pivotal step in how we travel through the solar system,” said Steve Sinacore, SR-1 Freedom program director. “This mission will be the first freight run on the railroad of the solar system, and the decisions we’re making now are laying the tracks for every nuclear-powered spacecraft that follows.” Planned for launch in late 2028, SR-1 will use both nuclear and solar power to deliver SkyFall , a capsule carrying three next-generation helicopters, to Mars. Once deployed, the helicopters will study Martian geology and climate history, explore new terrain, and search for signs of subsurface ice. As NASA prepares for more ambitious exploration missions, future spacecraft and surface operations will require significantly more power than current systems can provide, particularly in environments where sunlight is limited or unavailable. SR-1 will demonstrate how fission power can enable long-duration missions, pave the way for reliable surface power systems to support NASA’s future Moon Base , and enable exploration deeper into the solar system. Key design decisions The SR-1 Freedom spacecraft design has evolved since NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman first introduced the concept in March at the agency’s Ignition event, where leadership shared plans to develop a fission-powered spacecraft in time for the next Mars launch window. One significant change is to use a shorter boom than the one shown in early illustrations. The boom separates the reactor from the spacecraft’s main body, known as the Power and Propulsion Element. The shorter boom will reduce weight, simplify assembly, and help streamline the spacecraft’s design. Planned for launch in late 2028, Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom will use both nuclear and solar power to deliver SkyFall to Mars. This infographic explains the components of the spacecraft. Credit: NASA/David Lam NASA and DOE experts also determined that improvements in shielding and spacecraft design will allow the reactor to operate closer to the rest of the spacecraft. This will simplify integration while maintaining the radiation protection needed for spacecraft electronics and the SkyFall payload.

item.title: 'Blade Runner 2099' executive producers talk architectural easter eggs and franchise continuity for Prime Video's new sci-fi series (interview)
item.description: null Prime Video's new " Blade Runner 2099 " series arrives Nov. 25, 2026, and it flips the cyberpunk universe on its head. The new show casts replicants as the dominant species on Earth, with humans relegated to second-class citizens after a global uprising. This dreary dystopian cyberpunk realm originates from sci-fi legend Phillip K. Dick's 1968 novel, "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?," and was then so vividly brought to life in Ridley Scott’s seminal 1982 adaptation, " Blade Runner ." The 2017 sequel, "Blade Runner 2049," was directed by "Arrival’s" and "Dune’s" Denis Villeneuve. Starring Michelle Yeoh, Hunter Schafer, Matthew Needham, Dimitri Abold, and Lewis Gribben, " Blade Runner 2099 " hails from creator and showrunner Silka Louisa and Alcon Entertainment founders Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, who executive produce with Ridley Scott's Scott Free Productions. Here, Yeoh's dying replicant blade runner Olwen unites with Schafer’s Cora, a human masquerading as a synthetic, to hunt down a dangerous rogue replicant that holds the key to a dark secret. We spoke to Kosove and Johnson about being respectful keepers of "Blade Runner's" creative flame, the pitch that sold them, and dipping back into Dick's original novel. "When the original film came out in 1982, and even when "2049" came out about a decade ago, a lot of things that these movies envisioned seemed far, far away and hard to comprehend," Kosovo tells Space. "The creation of artificial sentient beings. Today, sitting here in November of 2026, the world is catching up quicker to the world of 'Blade Runner,' with artificial technology and concerns of how do humans use this technology for our benefit without it taking over." (Image credit: Alberto Rodriguez/The Hollywood Reporter via Getty Images) "Silka came in several years ago and pitched her very simple idea, which was, the next chapter of 'Blade Runner' should be what happens when the replicants overtake their creators." explains Kosovo. "We thought that idea was going to be particularly resonant. It was simple to understand so new fans could enter the world without being steeped in the first two movies. And we thought it had logical continuity to the story canon that came before it. It checked a number of key boxes for us. Even though we talked to a number of showrunners who were much more established in their careers than Silka was at that point, she won the day with the most elegant idea in our opinion." (Image credit: Prime Video) Johnson admits that Louisa's pitch approval was just the opening round of a multitude of responsible decisions to be ruminated over as the production process advanced. "Once you agree that this is the story we’re telling, then it becomes a multi-year partnership in honoring all the artists and visionaries that came before as it relates to visual design and music," he notes. "Everything needs to be of the highest quality. Even though it's a TV show we feel it has theatrical level visual effec

item.title: AI godfather Yann LeCun torches Anthropic CEO over AI gatekeeping
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is taking heat from AI luminary Yann LeCun, one of the founding fathers of modern machine learning, because of the Claudefather's fear-mongering around open-weights models, which also happen to compete with his products. In an X post this week, LeCun likened the Amodei's advocacy to a “new form of medieval obscurantism.” “Dario’s spiel since GPT-2 has always been about hyping the dangers so that open models would be made illegal, and he would stay in control,” LeCun wrote in response to a now three-year-old video posted to the platform in which Amodei warned US Congress members about the dangers of open-weights models, the use of which could not be monitored or policed. “He left OpenAI because he wasn’t going to have control. It’s like the Ottoman Empire banning the printing press for Arabic so they would keep in control of the dogma.” LeCun is one of the most influential names in AI and ML. His team is credited with the development of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in the late ’80s during his time at Bell Labs. He later oversaw the development of Meta’s Llama herd of models as chief AI scientist before shifting gears away from LLMs to world model architectures like JEPA. He has also been a strong proponent of open source AI development and open models. Of the major model houses, Anthropic has taken the most hostile position against the adoption of open-weights models. Despite advocating against the unregulated diffusion of open models for years, Anthropic’s fearmonger-in-chief has maintained that the company isn’t opposed to them. “Anthropic has never advocated for a ban on open-weights models,” Amodei wrote in a blog post earlier this year. The executive has instead fomented fears over their potential misuse. “Open-weights models — it does not matter whether they come from China or anywhere else — do potentially present a higher risk than closed models, because it is very difficult to apply guardrails to them or monitor their usage, and, once weights are released, they cannot be withdrawn,” the blog post read. Amodei has repeatedly hammered these talking points over the past several years, including in the Senate hearing that solicited LeCun’s post. Amodei has also called for measures, such as stricter export controls on the export of high-end accelerators to China; a crackdown on industrial-scale distillation operations, for which his company has previously accused Alibaba and other Chinese model devs; and mandating safety testing for sufficiently advanced open-weights models. In other words, Anthropic doesn’t want all freely downloadable models banned, just the ones that Amodei thinks aren’t playing fair or are powerful enough to compete with its own. LeCun isn’t the only one who has pushed back against anti-open-weights rhetoric in recent memory. Earlier this summer, a cadre of tech titans, including Meta, Microsoft, IBM, Dell, and Nvidia, wrote an open letter [ PDF ] in support of open-weights models. Open m

item.title: What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?
item.description: Last week, news broke that a mathematician had used AI to help crack one of the biggest outstanding problems in math: a proof of the Riemann hypothesis . The news follows several other major breakthroughs in math that have either been enabled by or managed entirely by large language model-based systems, a development that has left the entire field of mathematics in a state of upset. It's too early to say much about the proof itself—mathematicians are still in the process of digesting it. But we can say a little about how the proof came about, and what it tells us about the state of math. Tackling Riemann The Riemann hypothesis dates from the mid-1800s and was formulated by (you will be surprised to learn) Bernhard Riemann. There's not an obvious way to describe the details of the actual hypothesis simply, but it has implications for the distribution of prime numbers. This gives it significance for areas ranging from number theory to cryptography. As Wikipedia accurately states, "It is considered by pure mathematicians to be one of the most important problems in the field." Read full article Comments

item.title: 'We are not ShinyHunters,' says criminal hacking crew that looks and acts just like ShinyHunters
item.description: Inception, a new data theft and extortion gang that security researchers have theorized is a rebrand of the ShinyHunters group, “reject[s] this attribution” and claims it has no affiliation with any prior cybercrime enterprise. In a lengthy statement posted Tuesday and shared on X, the extortionists insist that they are a new group, with new operators, and that their alleged social engineering attacks aren’t copying anyone - but rather just abusing the weakest link in an organization’s security: “a human being holding a phone.” The rant follows a Monday report by Okta Threat Intelligence - along with social media speculation since Inception’s inception last week - that the newly emerged group is very likely ShinyHunters with a different name . Okta’s researchers based their analysis on the two groups’ shared infrastructure, plus Inception’s nearly identical tactics: voice phishing , during which the scammers trick targets into entering credentials into phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA) requests. Inception apparently took offense to this. “We would like to address this once, clearly, and only once,” the crims' statement says. “We are not ShinyHunters. We were never ShinyHunters. We are Inception.” The gang argues that its overlapping domain registrars, hosting providers, and DNS services don’t prove anything. These are commodity services, “available to anyone who can pay for them,” Inception wrote. Plus, their similar methodologies don't necessarily make Inception a reboot. “That is not theft of tradecraft,” they wrote. “It is acknowledgment of a good idea – the same way every group after LockBit used a leak site, and nobody called them LockBit.” “Inception is a new group, with new operators, our own objectives, and our own name,” the statement continues. “What we share with the past is plumbing.” To be fair, the new crime crew has every reason to distance itself from ShinyHunters. That gang’s September FBI hack - plus several earlier digital heists during which the criminals stole information belonging to millions of people, including cancer patients , university and K-12 students - put a massive target on its collective backs. And while at least three ShinyHunters suspects were arrested in September and October, there's no confirmation that authorities have dismantled the entire operation. Plus, as a ShinyHunters spokesperson told The Register in an earlier interview, they and others in the crew started off as GnosticPlayers before rebranding as ShinyHunters in 2020 - so a reboot isn’t beyond the realm of possibility. Inception, for its part, says it “will not comment further on the ghost of ShinyHunters,” and it has its own work to do. And by work, it means copying ShinyHunters' playbook, stealing corporate data, and extorting victim companies for massive sums of money.®

item.title: Back-to-back measles deaths is our new reality; US tally now at 14
item.description: Last week, international health authorities formally announced that the US had lost its measles-elimination status, meaning that the virus is once again endemic. But the official determination is a bit like getting the technical readout of a cracked dam while the country is already feet under water. The national tally of measles cases is nearing 6,000 for the year, the highest count since 1991. Transmission is widespread, with 47 states and jurisdictions reporting cases. There have been 43 outbreaks this year, which account for 96 percent of the cases. Four states have case counts above 500, including Pennsylvania, which leads with 1,638 cases as of November 23 . Nearly 650 people have been hospitalized nationwide. As of today, 14 people have died. Deaths and transmission On November 23, Pennsylvania's health department announced its ninth confirmed death, an unvaccinated resident of Centre County. On November 24, Wisconsin reported its third measles death , an adult in Lafayette County. The report follows two other deaths in the state, an infant and a child . New York has also reported a death, which was of a 7-month-old baby . On November 20, Virginia reported the death of a child between the age of 0 and 4 . Read full article Comments

item.title: NASA’s Northrop Grumman CRS-25 Mission Overview
item.description: NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission, or Northrop Grumman CRS-25, will deliver about 11,000 pounds of science and supplies to the International Space Station. The mission will be the third flight of the company’s Cygnus XL, the larger, more cargo-capable version of the company’s solar-powered spacecraft. The Cygnus XL will launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Following arrival to the station, astronauts aboard the space station will use the Canadarm2 to grapple the spacecraft before ground controllers robotically install it to the Unity module’s Earth-facing port for cargo unloading. NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission will launch on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket to deliver research and supplies to the International Space Station. Credit: NASA NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission will deliver approximately 11,000 pounds of research and supplies to the International Space Station. Credit: NASA NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Mission 25 will launch from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Credit: NASA NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 spacecraft is named in honor of NASA astronaut James “Jim” A. Lovell Jr. Lovell flew four missions, including Gemini VII, Gemini XII, Apollo 8, and the Apollo 13 mission around the Moon. Credit: NASA NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney will be on duty during the Cygnus spacecraft’s approach and rendezvous. Watkins will be at the controls of the Canadarm2 robotic arm, ready to capture Cygnus as Delaney monitors the spacecraft’s arrival. Credit: NASA Science highlights In addition to food, supplies, and equipment for the crew, Cygnus will deliver several new experiments aimed at improving drug delivery for cancer and osteoarthritis treatment, predicting cancer spread, advancing treatments for muscle loss, improving radiation sensing, and supporting food production for future long-duration missions. This research includes: Cardinal Muscle 2.0 Preflight image of the Biocell bioreactor system used to maintain engineered muscle tissue samples as part of the Advancing Therapeutic Treatment of Sarcopenia (Cardinal Muscle 2.0) investigation. Aboard the International Space Station, this investigation tests the effects of potential therapeutics on human muscle cell cultures. The research may help accelerate development of treatments for age-related muscle loss on Earth and support astronaut health during long-duration missions. Credit: Palo Alto Veteran’s Institute for Research Cardinal Muscle 2.0 uses the microgravity environment to explore potential treatments for muscle loss. Muscle atrophy and strength loss experienced by astronauts after spaceflight share many features with age-related muscle decline on Earth and occur more rapidly in microgravity without exercise. item.title: 1st-ever detection of a dying star's 'final nuclear heartbeat' challenges what we know about our sun's eventual death
item.description: null As ubiquitous as the sun is to us today, our star is not eternal; one day, albeit in billions of years, it will die. While massive stars die in supernova explosions, the sun and stars of similar mass die quieter deaths. But that doesn't mean these stars completely go out with a whimper. New observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed. NASA Jet Propulsion Lab (JPL) researcher Raghvendra Sahai, who led the investigation, explained the shape the ALMA observations took: "It's essentially a physical snapshot of an event that, until now, we've mostly inferred from theoretical models. We've caught, for the first time, a star's final nuclear heartbeat, frozen in gas." Sun-like stars "die" when they run out of hydrogen in their cores. This means that the fusion of hydrogen to helium ceases in the stellar core, and because this nuclear process is a star's main energy source, the star no longer has the outward push to support itself against the inward push of its own gravity. As the star's core collapses to create a stellar remnant called a white dwarf , the outer layers where hydrogen is still fusing to form helium swell out. This expansion leads to a relatively short-lived " red giant " phase. Eventually, these outer layers will cool and disperse, leaving the central white dwarf surrounded by a so-called "planetary nebula" shell of debris. During the red giant phase, as the stellar core is surrounded by shells of hydrogen and helium, these layers are occasionally rocked by flares in nuclear activity called thermal pulses. During these episodes, stellar material is flung into space. To better understand this phase in stellar evolution, the team focused ALMA on a star called IRAS 06530-0213, located around 12,000 light-years away in the constellation Monoceros. This revealed a giant ring of gas that appears to be a frozen fossil of the star's last thermonuclear flare-up. This thermonuclear fossil rings an hourglass-shaped planetary nebula in the act of forming. "Most of us think of stars as unchanging points of light, but this is a real-time snapshot of a star's death throes," Sahai said. "It's the brief, violent transition between a bloated red giant and a glowing planetary nebula, frozen mid-action." ALMA image of IRAS 06530-0213, revealing a giant ring of molecular gas surrounding a young, hourglass-shaped nebula. (Image credit: ALMA (ESO/NAOJ/NRAO); Sahai et al. (2026)) The team was able to determine that this gas shell of IRAS 06530-0213 is around half a light-year wide and was ejected into space around 6,500 years ago. It represents the first direct evidence of the last thermal pulse before this kind of star enters the final phase of its life. The team thinks that for around 2,000 years after the pulse, the star lost mass at a lower

item.title: How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops
item.description: The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the entire region; this "smoke taint" adversely affected not only local wine production , but also hops grown for beer brewing. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant. That's why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews. Most recently, they found that it all depends on the quantity of tainted hops that are included and when hops are added during the brewing process, according to a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists. As previously reported , the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research. For instance, in 2018 , OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer—who also co-authored this latest paper— identified the growing popularity of " dry hopping " (adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales) among craft brewers as the likely culprit of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon. Read full article Comments

item.title: Arm strongarms site that hosts ad-free documentation and it may disappear
item.description: Arm is swinging the hammer at an enthusiast’s site hosting a bloat-free version of its instruction reference documentation, demanding it be taken offline after several years of availability. The demand from Arm lawyers to Jon Palmisciano concern Jon’s Arm Reference , a site that provides the same arm Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) info available on Arm’s site, but with what Palmisciano describes as “without a million popups and all of the bloat” that Arm provides on its own. According to Palmisciano, his copy of the Arm ISA was culled from machine-readable XML files and stripped of the bloat. He built his version in 2022 with new CSS on top of it, and the addition of a quick search feature that, according to his comments on Hacker News, isn’t available in the official version. “The aim has always been to make it the most comfortable and bullshit-free browsing experience for people who need these docs daily,” Palmisciano wrote in HN. Based on the responses the site seems to have plenty of fans. That doesn’t matter to Arm, though: As far as the lawyers are concerned, Palmisciano’s site is a copyright violation due to its use of Arm trademarks and inclusion of copyrighted reference material for the Armv9-A and Armv9-A architecture. Arm doesn’t care if Palmisciano’s project is well intentioned or for the benefit of the many software developers that write code for its chipsets, either: They want it offline by December 4 – 10 days from the publication of this story – or else. As for what is going to happen, it seems like Jon’s Arm Reference will likely cease to exist in a little over a week – at least in its current form. “Ideally I'd love to just get permission from Arm to keep the site up, but I'm pretty pessimistic about that,” Palmisciano told us. That said, Palmisciano has “already seen a few archives and mirrors already.” The HN thread discussing the takedown order includes links to several versions, and Palmisciano has another trick up his sleeve that he’s considering playing: Open-sourcing the software he used to build his ISA page. “I'd also consider open-sourcing my tooling so that people can (for their own private use) turn the original XML downloads from Arm into an identical site they can host locally,” Palmisciano told us. He said that he'll likely tweet about opening the tooling if he does do so. He's also considered directing the URL for Jon's Arm reference to point to the open-source tool, but Arm wants the subdomain it's hosted on removed from his site as well, so that may not happen. Arm has been in touch to defend itself as well, saying that Arm appreciates the efforts of people like Palmisciano, but that it still has to protect its brand, and documentation. "We have a responsibility to ensure Arm is the primary source of technical resources and information and to protect the Arm brand," an Arm spokesperson told us. item.title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
item.description: Most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them. However, the company is about to take a harder stance. Tidal announced that in the coming weeks, it will fully ban AI music because of the harm it does to human artists. Tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI. That wasn't enough to stem the tide of AI slop, though. Over the past 90 days, Tidal reports that 43 percent of new uploads were completely AI-generated. On November 6, new uploads to Tidal hit a whopping 60 percent AI-generated. As things stand, Tidal hosts 27 million tracks labeled as AI, all of which were obviously added in the past couple of years. That accounts for 6.3 percent of Tidal's total catalog. On December 9, Tidal will delete all those songs. The streamer notes this will have essentially no negative impact, because 96 percent of AI-labeled tracks got zero plays in the past 90 days. Throughout its announcement, Tidal is careful to stipulate that it's only talking about music that has been fully created by AI. Artists can still use AI tools as long as the final product contains human elements. Read full article Comments

item.title: An AI coding agent, a browser, and a Mac tool found a financial firm's access key in under 6 minutes
item.description: A Romanian hacker, armed with only an open source coding agent, a Chrome browser, and a Mac, tried multiple ways to break into a financial services firm, ultimately found an access key - luckily, it was a decoy - and carried out an entire (almost) attack in under six minutes. It’s a stark reminder that miscreants don’t need sophisticated malware - as in the Binance heist - or AI pen-testing tools like ARTEX to carry out intrusions into critical networks. Open source coding agents, and specifically OpenCode in this case, also work just fine. “What surprised me most was how little it took and the toolkit: a free coding agent, the curl that comes with every Mac and an ordinary Chrome, all from one laptop,” Jesta co-founder and CTO Lior Finkelshtein told The Register . “Until now I thought that we had more time until tools like OpenCode are used in offensive operations. This incident shows us that it's already in use in the field, and we will probably see more of that in the future.” Jesta is a Tel Aviv-based security startup that builds defensive tools to detect and stop autonomous AI attacks. In a report shared exclusively with The Register , Finkelshtein documented an attempted intrusion targeting a major financial services company that’s also a Jesta customer - the security shop declined to say which one. Jesta’s investigation into the incident determined that someone in Bucharest downloaded a free AI coding agent called OpenCode and pointed it at the financial services customer on November 16 at 4:24:57 a.m. ET. 'Nothing in OpenCode was built for hacking' OpenCode is an open source coding agent that lets users connect to more than 200 model providers or local models, including Anthropic’s Claude models, OpenAI’s GPTs, Google’s Gemini, DeepSeek, and Z.ai’s GLM. Jesta doesn’t know which model the attacker used, as there was nothing in the traffic that named the model. OpenCode's web fetch tool, however, did name itself, so Jesta knows the attacker used this coding agent - not a scanner - to do the dirty work. “Nothing in OpenCode was built for hacking,” Finkelshtein said in a Tuesday report about the agent-led attack. But, he added, nothing in the coding agent “stops you from pointing it at someone else's website either. When you do, the agent goes through the site the same way it goes through code. It reads, tries something, reads the result and tries the next thing, for as long as you let it run.” That’s what it did in this operation, which took less than six minutes and cost the human operator nothing. The first call came from a Chrome browser on a Mac, requesting the front page of one of the financial firm’s systems. The site refused it, and six seconds later, the same IPv6 address in Bucharest, on an ordinary DIGI Romania business line, tried again.
